Those pale fires burning in his wolf skull helm flickered with cold fury that pressed against the destroyed battlefield, and for an instant, that devastating Axiom stopped swinging.
THE Primordial Paradox smiled.
This was his moment.
He wasn’t the most powerful entity present.
He knew that with certainty!
Grimvault exceeded him tremendously.
Even Sammarthiel, the being he currently faced, possessed more Proterozoic Bones and Organs than he did.
In a direct confrontation of power against power, he would lose.
He would fall.
He would become another casualty of a battle.
But THE Primordial Paradox had never believed in direct confrontation.
Paradox was his Civilization.
Contradiction was his authority.
And the greatest contradiction of combat was this:the moment your enemy stopped paying attention was the moment they had already lost, even if victory still appeared to be within their grasp.
Sammarthiel’s beautiful and terrible features were turned toward where Vahrkosis had dissolved.
Those wings of burning and frozen swords had ceased their constant motion, thousands of blades suspended in configurations of shock rather than readiness.
His attention was divided between the horror of watching an ally unravel and the fury of recognizing that Naldine possessed capabilities none of them had anticipated.
That division was everything.
THE Primordial Paradox moved without sound.

His obsidian titanic form surged forward with speed that contradicted his massive size, Rhyacian Proterozoic power flooding through foundations that had been enhanced by something most beings couldn’t comprehend.
The Bounded Countable Infinity he’d obtained from Osmont blazed within his existence with blue light that wove through his authority!
He wasn’t merely Paradox anymore.
He was Paradox touched by Infinity.
He was contradiction given endless recursion.
He was the impossible made more impossible through forces that his Civilization had integrated rather than rejected.
His Proterozoic chest bone began to shine.
The light that emerged was something else entirely, illumination that seemed to exist and not exist simultaneously, brightness that was also darkness, visibility that was also concealment.
The bone pulsed with authority that declared its paradoxical nature to anything capable of perceiving such depths.
Sammarthiel sensed the attack one instant too late.
The Paradox Bearer turned from his observation of Vahrkosis’s fate, those twin blades of flame and frost rising in defensive configuration as he recognized that THE Primordial Paradox had moved.
But recognition wasn’t prevention.
Awareness wasn’t escape!
He could see the paradoxical light surging toward him and still be unable to avoid what that light represented.
"You dare-...!"
The words cut off as...Schrodinger’s Tomb enveloped him.
Its capabilities were actually rather simple.
The Target is enclosed in state of fundamental uncertainty.
Until observation occurs or the target breaks free through sufficient force, they exist in superposition of alive and dead simultaneously.
The longer they remain in this state, the more their existence becomes entangled with the paradox itself.
Extended exposure causes progressive dissolution of certainty regarding their own continuation!
It wasn’t a cage in the physical sense.
There were no bars, no walls, no boundaries that could be perceived through normal observation.
Instead, Sammarthiel simply became uncertain.
His form flickered between presence and absence, between continuation and cessation, between the alive state and the dead state without settling on either.
He was trapped in the space between outcomes.
And the longer he remained there, the more that space would consume what he understood himself to be.
THE Primordial Paradox observed his work with satisfaction.
Sammarthiel struggled within the Tomb, those six wings of swords attempting to cut through uncertainty itself, but you couldn’t cut what didn’t exist in definable form.
You couldn’t burn or freeze or destroy a state of being that was simultaneously every state and no state at all.
He should’ve never allowed this cage to form as he was powerful enough to evade it!
But he...was distracted.
And as of this moment...
Two Rhyacian Tier Proterozoic Scale entities were both out of commission.
THE Primordial Paradox floated grandly above the destroyed battlefield, his obsidian form radiating authority that declared his classification to all who could perceive it.
He didn’t possess Pulses.
He didn’t channel powers derived from Causes that formed Observable Existences.
But he possessed something that Pulses couldn’t replicate and overwhelming force couldn’t overcome.
He possessed understanding of contradiction itself.
Victory and defeat were merely states that observers assigned to outcomes after those outcomes had been determined.
But what happened when determination itself became uncertain?
What happened when the very concept of winning or losing became entangled with paradox that refused to resolve into either?
This battle was neither won nor lost.
He thought about what Paradox meant at its deepest levels.
Most beings understood contradiction as opposition.
Light against dark.
Life against death.
Victory against defeat.
They saw paradox as tension between states that couldn’t coexist, as problems requiring resolution rather than conditions to be embraced.
THE Primordial Paradox knew better.
Contradiction... was completion.
Light didn’t fight darkness as it moreso it defined it.
Life didn’t battle death...it required it.
And victory didn’t triumph over defeat; it existed only because defeat was possible.
This battle existed in that space between.
Not won and not lost, but simply continuing in uncertainty that favored those who understood uncertainty better than their enemies.
He turned his gaze toward Grimvault, toward that wolf skull helm with its burning pale fires.
What...would the ancient Primordial Architect do now?
Grimvault’s eyes flashed cold.
Noah observed the shift in that wolf skull helm’s pale fires, watched the amusement drain away and something far more dangerous take its place.
The Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect had been playing before.
But Vahrkosis was gone now, unraveled by Naldine’s Pulse.
Sammarthiel was trapped in paradoxical uncertainty, flickering between alive and dead without resolution.
Grimvault was alone.
And alone, he stopped playing!
His left hand rose with speed that should have been impossible for something so massive.
His palm faced outward, fingers spread wide as if preparing to grasp something that existed beyond physical perception.
The gesture held stillness that seemed almost reverent, a warrior preparing to unleash a weapon that had been waiting since before Observable Existence learned to observe.
Then his fingers began to move.
The first motion was a curling inward, each finger bending in sequence from smallest to largest as if he were grasping threads of reality itself.
His hand drew backward in a pulling motion, those invisible threads gathering in his palm like strands of causality being unraveled from the weaving that held them in place.
Noah’s gaze became heavy!
His palm rotated slowly, drawing a circle in the air that suggested reversal, regression, the unwinding of time flowing backward against its natural current.
The motion was ancient, gestures that seemed to have existed before gestures were possible!
Noah could see it!
He could see the threads!
That was the terrifying part.
He could actually see what Grimvault was grasping, could perceive the strands of causality being gathered in that armored palm, could witness the fundamental forces being prepared for deployment.
His enhanced Civilizational Access showed him exactly what was coming.
Grimvault’s fingers snapped outward in a flicking motion, releasing whatever he had gathered while simultaneously reaching toward something distant.
Then his hand closed into a fist, authority condensing!
His fist opened.
His fingers spread as fire would bloom from kindling, and his voice emerged with words that pressed against existence itself.
"Silurian Ember, First of Flames."
The air began to burn with light that shouldn’t have existed.
"I grasp the Thread.
I burn the Thread."
Colors that had no names blazed outward from his spreading fingers!
"What was shall be unwritten, what stood shall stand no more."
The light intensified until looking at it became difficult even for beings at Proterozoic classification.
"THE SILURIAN LIGHT."
BOOM!
The Pulse emerged in its full grandeur.
It wasn’t merely fire or light.

It was something that existed at the intersection of both while transcending either, a manifestation of THE Silurian Cause itself reduced to pale imitation that remained devastating despite its diminished state!

The brilliance roared outward from Grimvault’s extended hand like an emerging Cause, like the birth of an Observable Existence compressed into weapon form as it was directed towards...Naldine and THE Primordial Paradox!
Noah’s gaze became stern and somber.
This wasn’t playful anymore!
Grimvault had targeted both Naldine and THE Primordial Paradox with authority that would erase their causality entirely, would unwrite their existence until not even memory remained.
The light surged toward them in twin streams of impossible brilliance, each one carrying force sufficient to unmake beings who had survived eons of existence.
Naldine’s singularity-dotted eyes widened as she sensed death approaching.
Her fingers moved toward her Vihuela’s strings, but THE Cambrian Word required time she didn’t have.
The rewriting Pulse couldn’t intercept an erasing Pulse when the erasing Pulse had already been released!
THE Primordial Paradox’s obsidian form flickered with paradoxical light as he attempted to apply contradiction to what was coming.
But THE Silurian Light didn’t care about paradox.
It didn’t care about alive or dead states.
It simply erased, and erasure transcended the philosophical frameworks that Paradox operated within!
Both of them roared with defiance that couldn’t change what was approaching!
And then...
And then Noah appeared in front of Naldine.
And Ozymandias appeared in front of THE Primordial Paradox.
Both bodies moved simultaneously!
Noah positioned himself directly in the path of the Silurian stream targeting Naldine while Ozymandias blocked the stream targeting THE Primordial Paradox.
His expression was unfathomably calm.
Time seemed to slow as he looked at the blinding light of THE Silurian Light approaching his existence.
The brilliance filled his perception with colors that shouldn’t have been capable of existing simultaneously!
It was...beautiful, and it was truly terrifying.
It was..exactly what he’d been searching for.
He wasn’t one for sacrifices.
That had never been his nature.
He didn’t throw himself in front of attacks to protect others out of noble impulse or heroic instinct.
He wasn’t sacrificing himself right now, wasn’t offering his existence to preserve theirs.
That kind of thinking belonged to beings who didn’t understand what he understood about himself.
He wanted to see.
He wanted to feel what a Pulse was all about.
That...was how confident he was about his own existence.
If it was a terrifying adversity even more than the swing of Grimvault’s weapon, all the better.
If it carried force sufficient to trigger THE Crucible of Observable Rebirth at accelerations that exceeded what THE Octogenary Echo had provided, even better still.
But more than wanting to survive it, he wanted to know if he could take it.
In life, you had to do dangerous things if you wanted things to change drastically.
You had to take bigger risks if you wanted bigger rewards.
You couldn’t grow into something unprecedented by following safe paths that others had already mapped.
You had to step into the unknown and let the unknown do its worst.
And he...wanted things to change drastically.
The Hadean Bones throughout his body blazed brighter as THE Silurian Light approached.
Observable force surged through his existence in concentrations that exceeded anything he’d channeled before.
Quintessence Infiniforce flooded outward from his foundations in waves of multicolored brilliance that met the approaching erasure like a tide meeting a shore.
Could he take it?
He was about to find out.
"FOOL!"
Grimvault’s roar echoed across the destroyed battlefield with genuine alarm.
The Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect actually stepped forward as if he could recall what he had already released.
"I never intended to use THE Silurian Light on you!
There are too many unknowns if you are erased!"
But it was too late for intentions.
The streams of impossible brilliance had already crossed the distance.
The light touched both of Noah’s bodies simultaneously.
And existence...became unfathomably silent!

chapters.title: Chapter 5094: What Gives You The Right?! I
paragraphs: <Exerpt from an Echoes of THE First Cause>

"The adversity that breaks all others shall forge him. The hardship that ends all paths shall begin his. The Scales demand what the Scales demand, and he shall pay in currencies that have not yet been minted.
Three times shall he face the mirror of undoing. Three times shall he choose between becoming and unbecoming. Three times shall the answer be the same, and three times shall the answer be different.
In the end, which is also the beginning, the Infinite shall stand before the Undefined. And only one shall remain to tell the tale that no one shall hear.
This is an Echo of First Cause.
This is what shall come to pass, for it has already passed, and it shall pass again.
The wheel turns. The river flows. The question echoes.
He shall be the answer, or he shall be nothing.
Or he shall be the question that ends all answers."
There exists a term for those who find pleasure in pain.
Algophilist!

From the word algos, meaning pain, and philos, meaning lover. One who loves suffering. One who seeks agony not as means to an end but as the end itself. The sensation of hurt becomes indistinguishable from the sensation of joy, and they pursue both with equal fervor because to them, both are the same.
Noah Osmont...was not an algophilist!
Silence.

All of existence turned silent as for the first time, Noah became the target of a Pulse of The Scales. THE Silurian Light touched him, and in that instant, he understood what Alexander had felt when Beowulf tortured him across millions of subjective years. Every Existential Nociceptor within his existence activated simultaneously, every pain receptor screaming with immensity and entered territories that most beings couldn’t survive experiencing.
Pain.

Real pain. Not the cycles of destruction and rebirth that Grimvault’s weapon had provided. Not the shattering and reforming that THE Crucible of Observable Rebirth had transformed into fuel for advancement. This was something else entirely, agony that existed at the level ofcausalityitself, suffering that came from having your very existence told it should never have been.
And Noah defiantly felt all of it.

He didn’t defend or retreat. He didn’t channel Infinity or Observable force to resist what was happening. He wanted to feel this. He wanted to understand what a Pulse truly was, what it meant to have something derived from a Cause deployed against your existence. So he opened himself to the pain and focused through it with clarity that his previous transformations had provided.
His existence bellowed toward the Pulse in defiance.
What are you? What do you stand for?
HUUM!

The answer came in sensation. He felt himself being stared down by an unfathomable imperious gaze of endless potential, a presence so vast that his perception couldn’t find its edges.This was a Cause.

THE Silurian Cause itself, the First Ember that had ignited Observable Existences into being across the vastness of reality. The Pulse he faced was drawing power from that originating force, and when an entity was targeted by such a thing, they felt the immensity behind it.
The immensity of THE Silurian Cause.
It seemed that one could feel it and experience a semblance of it only when targeted for complete erasure. In that moment of tremendous pain, Noah understood what THE Silurian Cause actually was.

It was fire before fire existed. It was ignition before anything could burn. It was the spark! It had birthed Observable Existences, had provided the template for reality, had established the foundations upon which all current existence stood.
And it wanted him gone.
|Understanding Achieved.|
|You have experienced direct contact with THE Silurian Cause through exposure to THE Silurian Light.|
|This Cause represents: Primordial ignition. The authority to declare existence into being, and therefore, the authority to declare existence into unbeing.|
|Knowledge of this Cause has been seared into your foundations. You now possess comprehension of THE Silurian Cause at foundational level.|
|This comprehension may enable future derivations if sufficient resonance is established.|
And after he experienced this Cause, after that moment of understanding bloomed through his awareness, he began to feel what came next.
Every atom within his existence screamed.

They were set aflame by that terrifying fiery light, burned by authority that had ignited Observable Existences and could therefore extinguish anything within them. The light pressed against every particle of what he was with a declaration that expected obedience.
Be erased.
Disappear.
Your existence has never been and will never be.
BEGONE!
HUUM!

His cells screamed. His existence screamed. And all of this was happening in the span of an instant, destruction cascading through his foundations at speeds that objective time couldn’t properly measure. He could feel his causality beginning to unravel, could sense the threads connecting his past to his present to his future being grasped by that fiery authority and pulled apart.
With Noah at the center, cracks bloomed in four directions!
BOOM!

The fractures spread outward from his existence like lightning frozen in glass, extending toward horizons that didn’t exist in normal space. His unraveling was unraveling existence itself, Infinity responding to the erasure of its bearer by threatening to take everything else with it. The cracks stretched infinitely in four different directions, north and south and east and west, reality itself protesting what was being done to someone so thoroughly entangled with its foundations.
Grimvault went pale beneath that wolf skull helm.

Those pale fires in his empty eye sockets flickered! The ancient Primordial Architect shook his head at this scene, recognizing that collapsing every causality of the Infinity-bearer could have untold consequences that extended far beyond this battlefield!
Noah’s existence was roaring out in response to the unfathomable pain and unwinding of his very causality. Every part of what he was said no.
A declaration of absolute refusal that pressed back against the Pulse with authority that came from somewhere deeper than his current classification could explain.
His Quintessence Infiniforce said no.
His Observable Force said no.
His connection to Infinity said no.
THE First Tongue said no.
THE Infiniverse said no.

And then Noah heard something else. A voice that didn’t belong to any system or Civilization or cosmic force. A voice he recognized from years of hearing it call him to dinner, wake him for school, comfort him through nightmares that childhood had provided.
His mother.
"How dare you?!"
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5095: What Gives You The Right?! II
paragraphs: Amelia Osmont, THE Originator of THE Infinite Cause, raged from wherever she existed within THE Infiniverse. Her voice crashed through Noah’s awareness with fury, the primal anger of a mother watching something try to erase her child. How dare they try to unmake what she had carried for nine months? How dare they try to unwrite what she had raised through sleepless nights and double shifts and years of sacrifice?!
How dare they?!
At such a moment, Noah’s eyes released blinding beams of light.

He dared to ask the Pulse of The Scales, the Pulse backed by THE Silurian Cause, a question that no one had ever asked while being targeted for erasure. His voice emerged not as sound but as existence itself bellowing toward the force that was trying to unmake him.
"What gives you the right?!"
WAA!

What gave this Cause the authority to unravel his causality? His very being? Was this Cause grander than his Cause? Was THE Silurian Cause so absolutely superior to THE Infinite Cause that it could simply declare him nonexistent and have that declaration stick?

His body surrounded itself in radiant magma-like light as THE Silurian Light continued its assault, flames that should have been erasing him instead illuminating his defiance for all to witness. He raised both arms, his primary body and Ozymandias moving in perfect synchrony despite the agony they both experienced.
And he roared with all of his existence.
Words emerged that nobody but himself and the force of THE Silurian Cause would hear, a challenge issued not to Grimvault but to the Cause behind Grimvault’s Pulse.
"What makes your Cause grander?!"
His voice tore through the flames surrounding him.
"THE Infinite Cause gave its emergence to me! Can you say with Absolute Certainty that THE Silurian Cause is grander than THE Infinite Cause?!"
The magma-light flickered.
"That of the endless threads and weavings of Causality, of past, present, and future, THE Infinite Cause is not grander than THE Silurian Cause?!"
HUUM!

His existence shone with blinding blue gold light that pushed back against the flames trying to erase him. Instead of fighting against the Pulse itself, he pitted the force behind it against his own Cause. Not power against power. Not authority against authority. But certainty against certainty.

Could THE Silurian Cause say with absolute conviction that it would always be grander than THE Infinite Cause? Because Noah’s growth wasn’t done. His trajectory wasn’t complete. THE Infinite Cause had already produced a Seed of Observable Existence, had already demonstrated potential that rivaled what THE Silurian Cause itself represented.
Did it have absolute certainty?!
Could it prove, beyond any reasonable possible doubt, that THE Infinite Cause would never surpass it across the endless spans of future existence?!
HUUM!
A heavy silence came.

This silence was uncertainty. And if there was uncertainty, even the slightest doubt about the absolute superiority of one Cause over another, then THE Silurian Light couldn’t complete its erasure. It couldn’t unravel causality that might one day prove grander than its own origin. It couldn’t destroy potential that remained undefined.
"OOOH!"
Noah roared out with fervor as his voice permeated across existence, the sound of someone who had just challenged a Cause itself and found that Cause unable to answer with absolute conviction.
|Critical Interaction Resolved.|
|THE Silurian Cause behind THE Silurian Light cannot definitively and absolutely prove its sovereignty over THE Infinite Cause.|

|THE Infinite Cause has demonstrated trajectory of growth that makes future superiority possible, if not probable.Absolute certainty of permanent superiority cannot be established when one Cause continues to evolve while the other has already achieved its zenith.|
|Result: THE Silurian Cause cannot unravel THE Infinite Cause.|
|You have gained immunity from any unraveling force of causality derived from THE Silurian Cause and any Pulses of The Scales derived from it.|
|However.|

|THE Silurian Cause is and has been grander than THE Infinite Cause in current measurement. While you are immune to complete unraveling, the effects of THE Silurian Light are still expressed with terrifying immensity capable of destroying every particle of your existence.|
|This destruction triggers THE Crucible of Observable Rebirth.|
|This light is more than sufficient to continue undergoing endless cycles of destruction and reformation until your Hadean Organs and Bones complete their transformation.|
|Until your glorious evolution attains something new.|
|Persevere.|

Noah saw all these prompts as his body continued blazing with magma-like light. He felt the flames of THE Silurian Light scorch every cell and atom of his existence in an instant, fire that couldn’t erase but could still destroy. And in that same instant, boundless Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force and Infinity surged into the destruction, regenerating everything that had been burned before the next wave of flames arrived.
A nanosecond later, the same thing happened again.
And again.
And again.

Visually, it seemed like the magma-like light of THE Silurian Light was simply burning him, flames wrapping around his form in configurations of destruction that should have been lethal. But a blast of blue gold brilliance flashed every nanosecond, explosions of reformation cascading outward from his existence with rhythm that only those who understood what was happening could perceive. Each flash signified a cycle of destruction and rebirth. Each burst of brilliance meant brand new cells across Noah’s body, grander than what had existed a nanosecond before.
Ozymandias underwent the same transformation.

His titanic form blazed with identical magma-light, flames of THE Silurian Light scorching every particle of his existence while blue gold brilliance regenerated what was lost. Both bodies burned. Both bodies reformed. Both bodies grew stronger with every nanosecond that passed.
But as the nanoseconds accumulated, something became clear to everyone watching.
He wasn’t unraveling.

His causality remained intact. His existence continued despite being targeted by a Pulse that should have erased him entirely. THE Silurian Light burned and burned and burned, but the being it burned refused to be unwritten.
Noah’s eyes opened wide on both bodies.

He looked out through flames that wreathed his existence, his gaze locking with Grimvault who stared back with utter incredulity and astonishment. Those pale fires in the wolf skull helm burned brighter than ever, but they burned with confusion rather than confidence.
Noah raised his right hand into a fist with both bodies, that gesture of defiance declaring something that shouldn’t have been possible.
"Merely a Pulse of The Scales."
His voice emerged calm despite the flames still burning around him.
"Merely THE Silurian Light."
His fists remained raised.
"It seems that I am already immune to it."
BOOM!

His words battered all nearby existence like hammers striking reality itself. A Pulse couldn’t be denied. That was the fundamental truth that made Pulses so terrifying. They operated on levels that normal authority couldn’t touch, drew power from Causes that predated most current forces. Only another Pulse could potentially reverse or combat a Pulse!
But Noah hadn’t cast any Pulses.
So how was he alive?
How was his causality intact?
How was he still standing there with flames wreathing his existence, defiant and unbroken and growing stronger with every nanosecond that passed?

Nobody here knew that he hadn’t fought the Pulse itself. He’d fought the Cause behind it, had challenged THE Silurian Cause to prove its absolute superiority over THE Infinite Cause, and the Cause had been unable to provide that proof!
Naldine stared at him with a look of stupor.
In all her experience, across eons of existence among Primordial Architects and classifications that most couldn’t imagine, she couldn’t explain this. She didn’t know what this was!

WAA!
What gave this Cause the authority to unravel his causality?
His very being?
Was this Cause grander than his Cause?
Was THE Silurian Cause so absolutely superior to THE Infinite Cause that it could simply declare him nonexistent and have that declaration stick?
His body surrounded itself in radiant magma-like light as THE Silurian Light continued its assault, flames that should have been erasing him instead illuminating his defiance for all to witness.
He raised both arms, his primary body and Ozymandias moving in perfect synchrony despite the agony they both experienced.
And he roared with all of his existence.
Words emerged that nobody but himself and the force of THE Silurian Cause would hear, a challenge issued not to Grimvault but to the Cause behind Grimvault’s Pulse.
"What makes your Cause grander?!"
His voice tore through the flames surrounding him.
"THE Infinite Cause gave its emergence to me!
Can you say with Absolute Certainty that THE Silurian Cause is grander than THE Infinite Cause?!"
The magma-light flickered.
"That of the endless threads and weavings of Causality, of past, present, and future, THE Infinite Cause is not grander than THE Silurian Cause?!"
HUUM!
His existence shone with blinding blue gold light that pushed back against the flames trying to erase him.
Instead of fighting against the Pulse itself, he pitted the force behind it against his own Cause.
Not power against power.
Not authority against authority.
But certainty against certainty.
Could THE Silurian Cause say with absolute conviction that it would always be grander than THE Infinite Cause?
Because Noah’s growth wasn’t done.
His trajectory wasn’t complete.
THE Infinite Cause had already produced a Seed of Observable Existence, had already demonstrated potential that rivaled what THE Silurian Cause itself represented.
Did it have absolute certainty?!
Could it prove, beyond any reasonable possible doubt, that THE Infinite Cause would never surpass it across the endless spans of future existence?!
HUUM!
A heavy silence came.
This silence was uncertainty.
And if there was uncertainty, even the slightest doubt about the absolute superiority of one Cause over another, then THE Silurian Light couldn’t complete its erasure.
It couldn’t unravel causality that might one day prove grander than its own origin.
It couldn’t destroy potential that remained undefined.
"OOOH!"
Noah roared out with fervor as his voice permeated across existence, the sound of someone who had just challenged a Cause itself and found that Cause unable to answer with absolute conviction.
|Critical Interaction Resolved.|
|THE Silurian Cause behind THE Silurian Light cannot definitively and absolutely prove its sovereignty over THE Infinite Cause.|

|THE Infinite Cause has demonstrated trajectory of growth that makes future superiority possible, if not probable.Absolute certainty of permanent superiority cannot be established when one Cause continues to evolve while the other has already achieved its zenith.|
|Result: THE Silurian Cause cannot unravel THE Infinite Cause.|
|You have gained immunity from any unraveling force of causality derived from THE Silurian Cause and any Pulses of The Scales derived from it.|
|However.|
|THE Silurian Cause is and has been grander than THE Infinite Cause in current measurement.
While you are immune to complete unraveling, the effects of THE Silurian Light are still expressed with terrifying immensity capable of destroying every particle of your existence.|
|This destruction triggers THE Crucible of Observable Rebirth.|
|This light is more than sufficient to continue undergoing endless cycles of destruction and reformation until your Hadean Organs and Bones complete their transformation.|
|Until your glorious evolution attains something new.|
|Persevere.|
Noah saw all these prompts as his body continued blazing with magma-like light.
He felt the flames of THE Silurian Light scorch every cell and atom of his existence in an instant, fire that couldn’t erase but could still destroy.

And in that same instant, boundless Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force and Infinity surged into the destruction, regenerating everything that had been burned before the next wave of flames arrived.
A nanosecond later, the same thing happened again.
And again.
And again.
Visually, it seemed like the magma-like light of THE Silurian Light was simply burning him, flames wrapping around his form in configurations of destruction that should have been lethal.

But a blast of blue gold brilliance flashed every nanosecond, explosions of reformation cascading outward from his existence with rhythm that only those who understood what was happening could perceive.
Each flash signified a cycle of destruction and rebirth.
Each burst of brilliance meant brand new cells across Noah’s body, grander than what had existed a nanosecond before.
Ozymandias underwent the same transformation.
His titanic form blazed with identical magma-light, flames of THE Silurian Light scorching every particle of his existence while blue gold brilliance regenerated what was lost.
Both bodies burned.
Both bodies reformed.
Both bodies grew stronger with every nanosecond that passed.
But as the nanoseconds accumulated, something became clear to everyone watching.
He wasn’t unraveling.
His causality remained intact.
His existence continued despite being targeted by a Pulse that should have erased him entirely.
THE Silurian Light burned and burned and burned, but the being it burned refused to be unwritten.
Noah’s eyes opened wide on both bodies.
He looked out through flames that wreathed his existence, his gaze locking with Grimvault who stared back with utter incredulity and astonishment.
Those pale fires in the wolf skull helm burned brighter than ever, but they burned with confusion rather than confidence.
Noah raised his right hand into a fist with both bodies, that gesture of defiance declaring something that shouldn’t have been possible.
"Merely a Pulse of The Scales."
His voice emerged calm despite the flames still burning around him.
"Merely THE Silurian Light."
His fists remained raised.
"It seems that I am already immune to it."
BOOM!
His words battered all nearby existence like hammers striking reality itself.
A Pulse couldn’t be denied.
That was the fundamental truth that made Pulses so terrifying.
They operated on levels that normal authority couldn’t touch, drew power from Causes that predated most current forces.
Only another Pulse could potentially reverse or combat a Pulse!
But Noah hadn’t cast any Pulses.
So how was he alive?
How was his causality intact?
How was he still standing there with flames wreathing his existence, defiant and unbroken and growing stronger with every nanosecond that passed?
Nobody here knew that he hadn’t fought the Pulse itself.
He’d fought the Cause behind it, had challenged THE Silurian Cause to prove its absolute superiority over THE Infinite Cause, and the Cause had been unable to provide that proof!
Naldine stared at him with a look of stupor.
In all her experience, across eons of existence among Primordial Architects and classifications that most couldn’t imagine, she couldn’t explain this.
She didn’t know what this was!

chapters.title: Chapter 5096: Destruction and Rebirth! I
paragraphs: And at this time, as Noah underwent constant cycles of destruction and rebirth too fast to even be perceived, as his existence blazed with magma-light and blue gold brilliance in alternating rhythm that made his transformation accelerate beyond anything Grimvault’s weapon had provided, the system provided an update.
|THE Crucible of Observable Rebirth: Progress Update.|
|Current Catalyst: THE Silurian Light (Pulse-derived destruction at maximum intensity).|
|Rate of transformation has increased by factor of 47 compared to previous catalyst.|
|Hadean Transformation Progress Report:|
|Skeletal Structure:|
|Right Hand (THE Hadean Hand of Infinite Grasp): 100% Complete.|
|Right Arm (THE Hadean Arm of Infinite Reach - Radius, Ulna, Humerus): 100% Complete.|
|Left Hand (THE Hadean Hand of Infinite Will): 100% Complete.|
|Left Arm (Radius, Ulna, Humerus): 89% Complete.|
|Right Leg (Femur, Patella, Tibia, Fibula, Tarsals, Metatarsals, Phalanges): 78% Complete.|
|Left Leg: 71% Complete.|
|Spine (Cervical, Thoracic, Lumbar, Sacral, Coccygeal Vertebrae): 54% Complete.|
|Ribcage (12 pairs of ribs, Sternum): 48% Complete.|
|Skull (Cranium, Facial Bones): 39% Complete.|
|Pelvis (Ilium, Ischium, Pubis): 44% Complete.|
|Organ Systems:|
|Heart: 51% Hadean Saturation.|
|Lungs: 47% Hadean Saturation.|
|Brain: 58% Hadean Saturation (benefiting from connection to Ozymandias’s THE Hadean Mind of Infinite Calculation).|
|Liver: 41% Hadean Saturation.|
|Kidneys: 38% Hadean Saturation.|
|Overall Hadean Transformation: 64%.|
|Note: THE Silurian Light’s scorching destructive power will continue to be more than sufficient for complete Hadean transformation. You simply need to persevere.|
|Estimated time to completion at current intensity: 4 minutes, 17 seconds.|
|Additional Analysis: Anomalous Interaction Detected.|
|THE Silurian Light is designed to erase. THE Silurian Cause grants authority to declare existence into unbeing. To unravek causality. This is its nature. This is its purpose.|
|Your existence cannot be erased due to uncertainty regarding Cause superiority.|
|However, THE Silurian Light still seeks targets for its erasing authority.|
|Your Quintessence Infiniforce is redirecting this seeking.|
|Your Observable Force is guiding this authority.|
|THE Hadean Organ of Civilization is processing this power.|
|Result: THE Silurian Light is being channeled toward perceivable limitations within your existence rather than your existence itself.|
His existence...was burning brightly!
Noah turned his gaze away from Grimvault.

The flames of THE Silurian Light still wreathed his existence in magma-like brilliance, still scorched every cell and atom of what he was, still provided the catalyst for transformation that accelerated with every passing nanosecond. But the destruction had become background noise now, fuel for advancement rather than threat to survival. He could observe other things while his existence burned and rebuilt itself endlessly.

THE Primordial Paradox floated nearby, obsidian form intact despite the chaos that had unfolded. Sammarthiel remained trapped in Schrodinger’s Tomb, flickering between alive and dead without resolution.

Naldine stood where she’d been when he intercepted THE Silurian Light, her singularity-dotted eyes wide with an expression he’d never seen on her imperious features. She was staring at him like she didn’t know what she was looking at anymore!
Both were safe.
Noah turned back to Grimvault.

The Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect stood frozen in place, those pale fires in his wolf skull helm burning with intensity that suggested internal conflict beyond what his massive armored form displayed. He’d just watched his Pulse fail to erase someone it should have unmade entirely!
He’d just witnessed an impossibility that violated everything he understood about how Causes and Pulses functioned.
And now Noah was looking at him with eyes that blazed blue gold through flames that couldn’t erase him.
"Grimvault."
His voice emerged calm, as if he weren’t currently burning with the fire of a Cause that had birthed Observable Existences.
"I want... to thank you."
Those pale fires flickered with confusion.

"Many things today wouldn’t have been possible if not for you. When you arrived with your companions, I saw adversity in forms I hadn’t encountered before. When you swung THE Octogenary Echo, you provided force sufficient to trigger transformations. When you unleashed THE Silurian Light, you gave me contact with a Cause I needed to understand."
He raised one hand, flames dancing around his fingers as his existence continued its endless cycle of destruction and rebirth.

"You have been a vessel of adversity. A hammer that forged rather than destroyed. A fire that tempered rather than consumed. Everything you threw at me became fuel for advancement you couldn’t have predicted. Every attack you delivered accelerated growth you couldn’t have imagined. You came here intending to beat me to paste and collect my weavings for THE Wyld, but instead you became the instrument of my evolution."
His smile held no warmth.
"For that, I am genuinely grateful. You’ve completed your task well, Grimvault. You’ve served your purpose with magisterial excellence!"
His eyes turned cold.
"And now...you’re not needed anymore."
Grimvault’s pale fires blazed with fury that pressed against the destroyed battlefield.
"You incoherent fucking fool..."
Noah didn’t respond with words.
He responded with motion.

His right hand rose slowly, index finger extended, flames of THE Silurian Light still wreathing his form in magma-like brilliance. The gesture was simple, almost casual, nothing like the complex somatic movements that Naldine had demonstrated for THE Silurian Light or THE Cambrian Word.
He drew the lemniscate.

His finger traced the symbol of infinity in the air before him, a horizontal figure-eight that looped back upon itself endlessly. The motion was elegant in its simplicity. Where his finger passed, blue gold light remained, the symbol hanging in the air with brilliance that pressed against everything within range.

The somatic component of THE Infinite Light required nothing more than this. No complex gestures. No sequences of movements that needed to be memorized. Just the symbol that represented his Cause, drawn with authority that came from being the product of that Cause.
And then his voice emerged with the verbal component.
"Infinite Ember."
The lemniscate blazed brighter.
"First Spark of my emergence."
Blue gold flames began spreading outward from the symbol.
"I am the Thread. I am the Cause. What exists without the fire of painful birth shall know that fire now."
The flames intensified until looking at them became difficult even for beings at Proterozoic classification.
"Let causality regress. Let existence remember its emergence. Let all that stands without the pained spark of life return to the moment before that spark was possible."
His voice rose with tyrannical authority that pressed against Grimvault’s existence itself.
"THE INFINITE LIGHT."
BOOM!
The Pulse emerged.

It wasn’t like THE Silurian Light. It didn’t manifest as streams of targeted destruction or magma-like flames seeking specific victims. THE Infinite Light emerged as a form of massive and endlessly stretching blue gold flaming illumination that covered all space above for gigaparsecs, light that seemed to extend beyond what normal perception could measure.
The sky burned.

Reality itself seemed to ignite with brilliance that declared a new Cause had been expressed, a new Pulse had been born, a new authority had entered the catalogue of powers that could reshape existence itself. The blue gold flames stretched across distances that made the destroyed battlefield seem insignificant, covering space that most beings couldn’t traverse across lifetimes of travel.
And all of that pressure locked onto Grimvault.
|Pulse Activation: THE Infinite Light.|
|Source: THE Infinite Cause.|
|Wielder: Noah Osmont.|
|This Pulse burns with the fire of THE Infinite Cause, drawing upon every aspect of its origin to fuel its authority.|

|The fire of cellular division when two cells became one and then divided into countless more. The fire of metabolic combustion that sustained nine months of formation. The fire of first breath when oxygen flooded lungs that had never known air. The fire of first heartbeat when rhythm commenced and never stopped. The fire of first Mana when power entered a vessel that had known only mundane existence.|
|But more than physical fire, this Pulse burns with the fire of human experience.|

|The fire of a mother working double shifts while pregnant because her husband gambled away the rent. The fire of being born alone in a hospital room while the one who should have been there chose cards over his own child. The fire of growing up without certainty, without safety, without the assurances that privilege provides. The fire of choosing to become something more despite every circumstance demanding you remain nothing.|
|THE Infinite Light burns with the fire of painful emergence.|
|Effect: This Pulse seeks to unravel the causality of anyone who has not experienced the pained emergence of life.|

|Target will be transformed from what they currently are. Target will undergo eons of regression compressed into instants. Target’s existence and Civilization will unravel backward through every stage of their development until they reach the state of an embryo.|
|And then that embryo will split back into single cells.|
|And those cells will separate into the components that preceded their union.|
|Grimvault, THE Primordial Silence, has not experienced the pained emergence of life. He was formed through different processes.|
|He is a valid target.|

Such a terrifying blue gold light gathered above endlessly, gigaparsecs of burning brilliance condensing into focused intent that had only one destination. The sky itself seemed to descend as THE Infinite Light crashed downward toward Grimvault with force.
Noah stared coldly as his Pulse fell upon his enemy.

The Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect who had existed since before humanity learned to count, who had consumed civilizations, who had executed twelve Primordial Architects under THE Deliverance’s directive, who possessed ninety-four percent Proterozoic Bone saturation and four Proterozoic Organs and THE Silurian Light itself, now faced a Pulse born from origins he couldn’t share.
He hadn’t emerged through pain.
He hadn’t known the fire that came from a mother’s sacrifice and a father’s absence and a childhood spent surviving rather than thriving.
And THE Infinite Light demanded that fire for immunity.

chapters.title: Chapter 5097: Destruction and Rebirth! II
paragraphs: THE Infinite Light lashed downward with speed of glory!

Blue gold flames descended from gigaparsecs of burning sky, all that gathered brilliance condensing into singular intent that had only one destination. The light moved like a predator that had finally found prey worth consuming!

Grimvault raised his Axiom greatsword in defensive posture, THE Octogenary Echo blazing with authority that had shattered countless entities across eons of violence. But THE Infinite Light didn’t care about weapons. It didn’t care about classifications. It cared only about whether its target possessed the fire of painful emergence.
And Grimvault didn’t possess that fire.
The Pulse struck him.
"AAARRGH!"
The roar that emerged from beneath that wolf skull helm was unlike anything Noah had heard from the Calymmian entity.
This was the sound of someone experiencing something they’d never experienced before and finding it utterly unbearable!
Grimvault’s massive figure began to fluctuate.

His form, which had seemed so permanent in its armored immensity, started shifting through configurations that shouldn’t have been possible for a being at his classification. He appeared smaller for an instant, his armor hanging loose on a frame that had diminished. Then larger, proportions distorting as if his existence couldn’t remember what size it was supposed to be. Then smallest, a flickering glimpse of something that might have been youth if youth was a concept that applied to Primordial Architects.
He was undergoing changes from adulthood to infancy.

THE Infinite Light’s regression was taking hold, unraveling his causality backward through stages of development that his existence had traversed across eons. His Proterozoic Bones flickered with instability as the Pulse demanded they return to states before they’d been transformed. His four Proterozoic Organs pulsed erratically as the authority of THE Infinite Cause pressed them toward origins they’d long since surpassed.
But Grimvault was still a terrifying being at Calymmian.

His ninety-four percent Proterozoic Bone saturation provided resistance that lesser entities couldn’t have mustered. His four Proterozoic Organs generated force that pushed back against the regression even as it tried to claim him. And beneath all of that, his Civilization spoke words that weren’t words, sounds that predated sound, authority that fought against unbirth with everything it possessed.
His hand rose despite the fluctuations wracking his form.
Palm outward. Fingers spreading. The curling motion. The pulling. The rotation. The snap. The fist. The opening.
"Silurian Ember, First of Flames!"
His voice emerged fractured, shifting between deep and high as his existence flickered between states.
"I grasp the Thread! I burn the Thread!"
THE Silurian Light blazed outward from his spreading fingers, meeting THE Infinite Light in collision that warped reality itself around their intersection.
"What was shall be unwritten, what stood shall stand no more!"
Blue gold flames met magma-like brilliance in configurations that existence wasn’t designed to accommodate.
"THE SILURIAN LIGHT!"
BOOM!
The two Pulses clashed.

THE Infinite Light sought to regress. THE Silurian Light sought to erase. Both drew power from Causes that had birthed or would birth Observable Existences, and neither could claim absolute superiority over the other. The sky burned with colors that had no names as Pulse fought Pulse in displays that painted the destroyed battlefield in hues of glorious warfare.
But Grimvault knew he couldn’t sustain this.

His form still fluctuated despite THE Silurian Light’s counter. His existence still felt the pull of regression that THE Infinite Light demanded. He was buying time, not achieving victory. And time was running out as his Proterozoic reserves depleted faster than they could regenerate!
He made a decision.

His Axiom greatsword, THE Octogenary Echo, reversed in his grip. The blade that had been pointed outward turned inward, that light-drinking metal now aimed at his own armored chest. Without hesitation, without the careful consideration that beings at his classification usually employed, he drove the weapon into himself.
The Axiom pierced through blackened silver armor that had fused with his flesh.

It sank into his chest cavity. But he wasn’t trying to destroy himself. He was anchoring himself, using the multiplicative force of THE Octogenary Echo to replicate his current state eighty-one times in a single nanosecond, creating so many overlapping instances of his present existence that regression couldn’t find purchase!
Oh!
His form stabilized.

The fluctuations ceased. The shifting between sizes stopped. Grimvault stood anchored in his current state, Axiom buried in his own chest, THE Silurian Light still streaming from his other hand to counter THE Infinite Light that continued pressing against his existence.
But his eyes.
Those pale fires burning in his wolf skull helm’s empty sockets stared at Noah with fury and shock and something else.
Something that Calymmian entities weren’t supposed to feel when facing beings at THE First Scale.
Fear!
Because he knew now.

Whatever power Noah had utilized, which should somehow be a Pulse despite him having no right to possess one, could actually unravel him. Actually unravel him, regress his causality until his existence returned to states that preceded his current form, until his Civilization dissolved back into potential that had never been actualized.
Him!
A Calymmian Proterozoic Scale entity!
The realization pressed against his awareness with horror that made his Axiom-anchored form tremble despite its enforced stability!
Grimvault howled with rage that didn’t quite conceal the terror beneath it.
"This is not the last of it, you blue tinged Gamaidjan fucker!"
His voice boomed across the destroyed battlefield as he wrenched his Axiom from his own chest, blood the color of pale starlight leaking from the wound he’d inflicted upon himself.
"This is not done, Osmont!"
His free hand rose, fingers moving through gestures that had nothing to do with Pulses, words emerging in gibberish that wasn’t actually gibberish at all.
"IT IS NOT!"
BOOM!
Existence cracked.

The fabric of reality splintered before Grimvault’s speaking, fractures spreading outward from his position in configurations that resembled shattered glass. Through those cracks, something else became visible.
THE Interstices.
The corridors through existence that allowed travel beyond what normal motion could achieve!
Grimvault had torn one open right there on the battlefield, and he used it.

The Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect who had arrived with such confidence, who had issued commands expecting obedience, who had unleashed THE Silurian Light with certainty, threw himself through the crack in existence without looking back.
He ran!

The fractures sealed behind him, leaving no trace of the pathway he’d used to flee. THE Infinite Light chased after its target endlessly, and the sky in waves of blue gold brilliance gradually faded into the normal hues.
Silence fell across the destroyed battlefield as a Calymmian Proterozoic Scale entity had run away fearfully.
The multicolored rain resumed.

Heavy silence had hung across the destroyed battlefield in the moments following Grimvault’s retreat, existence itself seeming to hold its breath after witnessing what had just occurred. But THE Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity didn’t care about dramatic pauses. The rain that carried Noah’s and THE Creature’s authority returned with steady rhythm, droplets of multicolored brilliance pelting everyone present with persistence.
The raindrops vaporized when they landed on Noah and Ozymandias.

Magma-like light still burned around both bodies, flames of THE Silurian Light continuing their endless assault despite Grimvault’s departure. The Calymmian entity had fled, but his Pulse remained active, still scorching every cell and atom of Noah’s existence with fire derived from THE Silurian Cause. And with every passing nanosecond, blasts of blue and gold erupted outward from both forms, brilliant explosions of reformation that signified destruction and rebirth cascading through foundations that grew grander with each cycle.
Noah’s thoughts turned to Grimvault’s escape.

It was unfortunate, certainly. The loot of a Calymmian Tier Primordial Architect would have been extraordinary. Ninety-four percent Proterozoic Bone saturation. Four Proterozoic Organs. THE Octogenary Echo.
Missing out on such resources stung in the practical part of his mind.
But that entity had already given him the most profound loot he could.

This constant burning of a Pulse of The Scales, this endless cycle of destruction that THE Silurian Light provided, was worth more than Grimvault’s physical components. A Pulse that could eradicate Calymmian Tier entities was currently scorching him without pause. He was surviving it. He was using it to undergo evolution. Every nanosecond that passed brought him closer to complete Hadean transformation, and he had Grimvault to thank for providing the catalyst.
The escaping enemy had still served his purpose.

Noah closed his eyes to feel the cycles of destruction and rebirth flowing through his existence. Each wave of flame from THE Silurian Light annihilated everything he was. Each surge of Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force rebuilt what had been destroyed. The rhythm had become almost meditative now, destruction and reformation blending into continuous transformation that his awareness could observe without being overwhelmed by the agony it represented.
With every destruction, he felt Mana, he felt THE First Tongue break and reform into endless variations. He felt...Everything about him become grander!
He sensed Naldine still looking at him wordlessly.

Her singularity-dotted eyes hadn’t moved from his form since he’d survived THE Silurian Light and deployed THE Infinite Light in response. She stood there in the multicolored rain, droplets beading on her radiant white hair.
THE Primordial Paradox was the same.

His obsidian titanic form floated nearby, Sammarthiel still flickering in Schrodinger’s Tomb behind him. His gaze held profundity as he stared at Noah, ancient eyes processing implications that would take time to fully comprehend.
Off to the side, Alexander rose up.

His Enneagram pulsed with dangerous light, nine points blazing with authority that seemed more substantial than it had been before the battle began. Blood still stained his gloved hands from hours of work within Beowulf’s chest cavity. His face still bore streaks of crimson gold fluid that he hadn’t bothered to wipe away. But his expression held satisfaction.
When one looked at Beowulf, they understood why.

The massive Primordial Architect still hung suspended by nine spears, his body trembling and twitching in a daze. But something fundamental had changed. His network of Second Scale receptors and Nociceptors, that entire system Alexander had spent millions of subjective years studying through experiencing its torments, was gone.
Completely removed.

Transplanted into Alexander’s own body, integrated into foundations that would never forget what those receptors had been used for. The tortured had become the possessor of the instrument of torture. The victim had claimed the weapon that had been used against him!
Alexander looked toward Noah.

Noah nodded in acknowledgment, then waved his hands toward Beowulf’s suspended form. His will reached inward, touching THE Hadean Organ of Civilization that spun within his chest. A command was issued without verbal expression, authority directed toward the construct that made his impossible progression possible.
Another entrant into THE Hadean Desmoterion had appeared.
|Command Received: Imprisonment of external entity.|
|Target: Beowulf, THE Primordial Architect of Armed Existence.|

|Current State: Heavily injured. Rhyacian Tier Proterozoic Scale. Network of Existential Nociceptors removed. Cognitive function severely impaired. Civilizational Anchor destabilized through prolonged torture.|
|Processing.|
The massive body of Beowulf began to dissolve.

His form, which had seemed so immense and threatening when he first arrived at this battlefield, turned into streams of crimson gold light that flowed toward Noah’s position. The nine spears that had anchored him joined into one. His armor, his flesh, his Proterozoic Bones, all of it converted into luminous streams that crossed the distance between where he’d been suspended and where Noah stood burning with magma-like flames.
The streams entered Noah’s chest.
They flowed into THE Hadean Organ of Civilization, into THE Hadean Desmoterion contained within where he would be joining Ozymandias and THE Living Elemental and all others in that internal space.
|Imprisonment Complete.|
|Entity: Beowulf, THE Primordial Architect of Armed Existence.|
|Classification: Heavily injured Rhyacian Tier Proterozoic Lifeform.|
|Location: THE Hadean Desmoterion.|
|Status: Contained. Civilizational development will resume shortly.|
Noah observed all of this as he breathed.

The cycles of destruction and rebirth continued without pause, THE Silurian Light still burning, blue gold brilliance still erupting with every nanosecond. But the battle was over now. The enemies were dealt with. Vahrkosis had been unraveled by Naldine’s Cambrian Word. Sammarthiel remained trapped in Schrodinger’s Tomb. Grimvault had fled through THE Interstices. Beowulf was imprisoned within his own existence.
Now he could simply focus on experiencing the cycles until their final culmination.

Both his bodies floated toward each other, the titanic form of Ozymandias and the smaller frame of his primary existence moving until they positioned back to back. They began to spin slowly, rotating in perfect synchrony as blasts of blue gold erupted around them in rhythm with the nanosecond cycles of destruction and rebirth.
All around them, seas of Observable Force gathered.

The connection to Eon continued flooding golden light into his existence at rates that made rivers seem like trickles. Quintessence Infiniforce generated endlessly within his foundations, providing resources that the transformation required. Infinity across Observable Existence responded to what was happening, his claims scattered throughout reality channeling support toward his evolution.
The multicolored rain fell.
The flames burned.
The cycles continued!
And across Observable Existence, a few beings who had witnessed what just occurred processed many implications.
It was the end of a shocking conflict that made one thing horribly clear.

Osmont, THE Infinity-bearer, had been attacked by a Calymmian Proterozoic Scale entity with a Pulse of The Scales. He’d been targeted for complete erasure by THE Silurian Light, the same authority that could unmake causality itself and erase beings until not even memory of them remained.
And he wasn’t affected.
He’d even proclaimed immunity!
This...held far too many conclusions to draw.

chapters.title: Chapter 5098: Destruction and Rebirth! III
paragraphs: <Fragment of awareness attributed to THE Deliverance>
In spans that predated the concept of spans, THE Deliverance had observed the nature of advancement with attention that most beings could not sustain across even a fraction of such duration.
It had watched countless existences conflate two processes which were, upon examination that required no effort for something of its nature, quite fundamentally distinct from one another.
Transcendance and Ascension.

Transcendence referred to the elevation of existence beyond its current categorical limitations, the movement from one classification to another in ways that redefined what the being fundamentally was. Ascension represented advancement within one’s existing classification, the refinement and expansion of capabilities without actually changing the foundational nature of the existence in question.
The distinction mattered. Those who failed to understand this failed at everything that followed.

A Primordial Architect who forged additional Proterozoic Bones, who cultivated new Organs, who progressed from Rhyacian to Calymmian to Ediacaran, this being was ascending. They grew more powerful. They remained what they always were. Their classification did not change; only their position within that classification elevated.
THE Deliverance had observed this process unfold across eons beyond counting, had watched beings celebrate advancements that changed nothing fundamental about their nature.
He had been foolish enough to ask before...if one desired to transform from THE Bounded status to THE Gilded status, would such a transformation be considered transcendence?
The asking itself long ago revealed his own fundamental misunderstanding of how existence had been woven.
It was not possible to transform from Bounded to Gilded.

This was not difficulty or a ceiling. The distinctions between Bounded and Gilded were established permanently, and those distinctions were permanent by design. They were not limitations to be overcome. They were definitions.One did not transcend a definition; one simply was or was not what the definition described.

Even if a Gilded Lifeform sealed themselves to live as Bounded. They walked among those they were engineered to surpass. They experienced limitations never meant for them. Even when they forgot what they truly were.
But forgetting changed nothing.

The seal suppressed expression. It did not alter engineering. Remove the seal, and what was always there reasserted itself. The Bounded lifeform beside them could remove a thousand seals and would remain precisely what they were at first breath:Bounded.
Limited by design. Constrained by intention that predated their existence by margins they could not comprehend.
This truth simply was. And those who failed to understand it would continue failing, as they always had, as they always would, until existence itself concluded its long and patient turning.

Existence breathes, and epochs pass, leaving Civilizations that become monuments, then crumble to memory, and are long forgotten when that breath comes again. In all these epochs, Infinity reigns supreme.
The entire region had transformed into something...unimaginable.

Tumultuous primordial seas of gold Observable Force stretched in every direction, waves crashing against waves in configurations that had nothing to do with gravity or current. Multicolored Quintessence Infiniforce wove through those golden seas like rivers of impossible light threading through an ocean that shouldn’t have existed.
The destroyed battlefield was gone now, replaced by this churning expanse of raw authority that had gathered in response to what was occurring at its center.
Typhoons bloomed across the surface of these seas.

Storms of Observable Force twisted into spiraling columns that reached toward heights that most beings couldn’t perceive, their rotation carrying enough power to obliterate Absolutes who strayed too close. Lightning made of Quintessence Infiniforce arced between the typhoons, connecting them in networks of multicolored brilliance that painted the entire region in hues of transformation and genesis.
And at the very center of it all, Noah could feel his body undergoing the last cycles of destruction and rebirth.

It was taking longer and longer for THE Silurian Light to be capable of destroying his atoms and cells. Dozens of nanoseconds before this, he’d actually had to release any natural passive defenses, consciously lowering the resistance his transforming existence had developed. Otherwise, he might not have been able to undergo the cycles of destruction at all. The fire that had once threatened to erase him entirely now struggled to even damage cells that had been rebuilt so many times they’d forgotten what weakness felt like.
But finally, after cycles beyond counting, after transformation that had compressed eons into minutes, the moment arrived.
BOOM!
The magma-like light blazed for one last moment.

It pressed against his existence with everything it had remaining, that fire derived from THE Silurian Cause attempting one final assault on foundations that had grown too grand for it to damage. The flames cried out as if giving up, a sound that wasn’t sound but rather the sensation of authority recognizing its own inadequacy.
And everything about it faded.

THE Silurian Light, the Pulse that Grimvault had unleashed to erase him, the fire that had scorched his existence through countless nanoseconds of destruction and rebirth, simply ceased. Its purpose had been exhausted. Its power had been absorbed. Nothing remained but the aftermath of what it had catalyzed!
Noah floated at the center of the primordial seas with his eyes closed.

His body still burned with residual heat that had nothing to do with the departed Pulse, warmth generated by transformation that was reaching its culmination. He raised his hands up, palms facing the churning sky of Observable Force that stretched above this impossible region.
HUUM!
His last cycle of destruction displayed itself to all who were watching.

His entire body broke apart into pure particles of Infinity and Observable Force, form dissolving into components so fundamental that they preceded the concept of form itself. Ozymandias underwent the same dissolution simultaneously, that titanic frame shattering into brilliance that matched what Noah’s smaller body had become.
A blinding light bloomed across the primordial seas.
Even Alexander turned his eyes away from what he was witnessing. Naldine, who had observed phenomena across eons of existence among Primordial Architects, shielded her singularity-dotted gaze!
THE Primordial Paradox shifted his obsidian form away from the epicenter!
The light folded back.
Particles of Infinity and Observable Force that had scattered across the primordial seas began converging, drawn together.

They coalesced with purpose that declared their destination, streams of brilliance flowing toward a central point where form was being reconstructed from components that had been purified through cycles beyond counting.
Noah’s body emerged from the convergence shining unfathomably gold.

His hair now radiated with multicolored light that shifted through hues as his existence settled into its new configuration. The strands seemed to contain depths that normal hair couldn’t possess, each one blazing with Quintessence Infiniforce that had been integrated so thoroughly it had become part of his physical appearance.

His fair skin illuminated from within, golden light pressing outward through flesh that had been rebuilt at the subatomic level. The illumination wasn’t harsh or aggressive. It simply was, the natural consequence of foundations saturated with Observable Force at densities that Bounded classification shouldn’t have been able to contain.
And for a moment, momentarily visible to Naldine and all others present, the outline of his internal structure revealed itself through that illuminated skin.
An entirely crystalline multicolored golden skeleton.

Every bone blazed with brilliance that declared its transformation complete, structures that had once been mundane now existing as something that exceeded Proterozoic classification entirely. The skull. The spine. The ribcage. The pelvis.
Every arm bone and leg bone and hand bone and foot bone, all of them shining with authority that made the Proterozoic Bones of fallen Primordial Architects seem dim by comparison!
And apart from the skeleton, there were radiant crystalline Organs.
His heart pulsed with golden light that pressed outward through his chest. His lungs expanded and contracted with brilliance. His brain blazed brightest of all!
The massive obsidian form of Ozymandias had undergone similar transformation.

That titanic frame now radiated with the same golden brilliance that Noah’s smaller body displayed, crystalline structures visible beneath flesh that had been rebuilt through the same cycles of destruction and rebirth. Where there had been one transformed body, now there were two, both shining with authority that exceeded what THE Second Scale was supposed to represent.
Noah opened his eyes.
The simple act felt like the opening of ancient doors, lids rising to reveal what lay behind them with significance that pressed against all surrounding authority!
HUUM!

The primordial seas trembled. The typhoons of Observable Force stuttered in their rotation. The lightning of Quintessence Infiniforce paused mid-arc as if waiting to see what those newly opened eyes would observe.
He raised his hand and looked at himself.
He felt brand new. Brand new, as if he’d never existed before this moment, as if everything that had come before was merely preparation for what he had just become.
And just by raising his hand...
HUUM!
His movement was accompanied by terrifying force that he hadn’t consciously intended. A blinding gold brilliance erupted from the simple gesture, nearby existence twisting in response!

A beam of golden light tore across space from his raised fingers, carving through the primordial seas with power that could have caused a Rhyacian Proterozoic Lifeform like Beowulf to go pale with terror!
He...hadn’t meant to do that.

He stopped any movements immediately, recognizing that his new existence required calibration he hadn’t yet performed. His eyes closed again as he turned his attention inward, seeking to sense the changes that had occurred through cycles of transformation he’d lost count of long ago.
The prompts rained down as they felt...sublime. Ruination’s voice and words felt sublime!
|You have become a Hadean Lifeform. THE Hadean Lifeform.|

|You remain, in apparent terms, at THE First Scale, having not yet formally established your Civilizational Anchor through the traditional methodology of affirmation.
