Infinitas Corpus, Infinitas Architectura, Infinitas Causa.
Three demarcations.
One Pillar.
Unlimited potential.
And right now...
"I have been stuck on this level for too long."
Noah’s voice emerged with conviction that pressed against the surrounding environment.
"Has it already been a day?
A few days?
Far too long!"
His eyes blazed brighter as he rose from his seated position.
"I shall advance toward Infinitas Architectura where Absolute Infinity awaits."
HUUM!
The island he occupied began to tremble beneath forces that transcended physical causation.
He rose from the grassland and floated upward, his body lifting through air that grew thicker with authority as he ascended.
He rose to the midpoint of this realm, that space where the endless blue sea below mirrored the endless blue sea above.
Two oceans stretching infinitely in opposite directions, and he floated between them like a singular point of purpose suspended in aquatic infinity.
His eyes were unfathomably bright as he considered what he was about to attempt.
So far, it was just ideas.
Even though they were ideas he had refined through nine iterations of careful design, nobody had told Noah they would work.
They might succeed brilliantly.
They might fail catastrophically.
There was no precedent for what he was doing because no one had ever done it before.
He was a Pioneer.
He was carving this path himself, and if he went wrong anywhere, it would be very costly.

There were no teachers to correct his mistakes, no ancient texts describing how to construct a Hadean Pillar of Infinity, no accumulated wisdom from countless practitioners who had walked this road before him.
There was only him.
So...
"Infinitas Architectura."
He called out the name as his body began generating even more endless Quintessence Infiniforce.
Blue Infinity gathered all around him in concentrations that would have driven most beings to madness.
Observable Force formed into golden rivers that circled his position.
The construction of a singular internal structure that would serve as the foundation for everything that followed.
He would build a Hadean Pillar of Infinity within his existence.
Rather than constructing multiple separate pillars for different authorities, he would create a single Pillar that could be built up by as many Civilizations as he could actualize within it.
Each Civilization he congealed into stable form would become another layer of the Hadean Pillar of Infinity, another foundation stone supporting the structure he was building.
Observable Force would be the binding agent holding these actualized Civilizations together.
Quintessence Infiniforce would serve as the animating principle allowing them to function as a unified whole rather than separate fragments.
He made sure he understood everything well.
Then he took a step.
The motion seemed mundane.
One foot lifting, moving forward through space, descending toward a surface that existed only in concept rather than physical reality.
It was a step that anyone could take, a movement so basic that infants learned it within their first year of life.
But with this step, this entire realm became bathed in blue and gold and multicolored brilliance.
Infinite seas surged into that single motion.

Every drop of Observable Force he had access to, every mote of Quintessence Infiniforce his existence generated, every trace of authority he could muster flowed into the act of bringing his foot down.
When it landed, something within him shattered.
BOOM!
A barrier he hadn’t known existed broke apart, and what emerged from behind it defied description.
A single massive Pillar rose up from within his existence.
It stretched out in this realm first, its base forming somewhere in the depths of his Hadean Organ of Civilization before expanding outward in all directions.
The Pillar passed through this Oceanus-like domain without disturbing the twin seas above and below, its form somehow existing alongside physical reality rather than displacing it.
Then it stretched further.
Past other thousands of realms across THE Infiniverse, the Pillar extended.
Through territories that held sacred herbs and tumultuous seas and floating landmasses of every description.
THE Infiniverse trembled as this construct rose through her depths, her humanoid manifestation opening her eyes with surprise as something vast moved through her very being.
The Pillar rose out of THE Infiniverse entirely.
It emerged into THE Wastes.
The multicolored rain of THE Pluvial Epoch fell upon its surface as it continued stretching upward, higher and higher, showing no signs of stopping.
Infinitely.
The Pillar was grand beyond comprehension, its surface blazing with multicolored light that shifted through every hue existence had ever named.
Golden bands wrapped around its circumference at irregular intervals, patterns of Observable Force that served as binding agents even as they contributed to its beauty.
But for all its grandeur, the Pillar was hollow.
Its interior waited to be filled.
The Civilizations that would form its layers had not yet been actualized.
The structure existed, but its contents remained potential rather than actual.
It was a monument waiting for meaning, a foundation waiting for what would be built upon it.
The Pillar crossed THE Wastes and continued rising.
It flashed momentarily in different Primordial Realms, its illusory form manifesting wherever existence permitted its passage.
Beings across countless territories looked up as something impossible bloomed across their skies, a Pillar that seemed to connect the lowest depths to the highest heights while belonging to neither!
It even manifested across Prima Indifferentia.

That region of Undivided Ones and Formless Terrors and Primordial Architects witnessed the Pillar’s passage through their domain, ancient consciousnesses stirring with confusion at something they couldn’t categorize.
The white gold sea that defined their home rippled with disturbance that had nothing to do with current or tide.
On this day, across Observable Existence, an Infinite Pillar bloomed momentarily!
Many witnessed it!
And they wondered.
What the fuck is that?!
THE Wyld stretched endlessly in ways that defied sanity.
This region existed as the true home of Primordial Architects, but "home" implied comfort that THE Wyld did not provide.
It was a realm of primal power and ancient danger, where the line between hunter and hunted shifted with each passing moment.
Survival here required strength that most beings couldn’t comprehend.
THE Creature stood within a forest that looked like something from primeval times.
Trees rose hundreds of meters high, their bark cracite with age of THE First Cause.
Branches intertwined overhead in canopies so thick that whatever passed for sky in THE Wyld remained invisible.
Bioluminescent fungi clung to trunks and roots, providing illumination that painted everything in shades of ethereal green and deep violet.
Abundant existential energy saturated every molecule of this forest.
Just breathing here would have advanced most First Scale beings through multiple stages of cultivation.
The concentration of authority pressed against everything with density that made the richest regions of normal Observable Existence seem impoverished by comparison.
This was why Primordial Architects thrived in THE Wyld despite its dangers.
The rewards matched the risks.
Milky gold rivers of light and blood flowed around the small clearing where THE Creature stood.
The liquid wasn’t water.
It was something between Observable Force and vital fluid, the runoff from conflicts that had occurred in this location recently.
Very recently!
The blood was still warm, still carrying traces of authority from beings who had been alive mere minutes ago.
Seven Primordial Architects lay scattered around the clearing.
Their bodies were arranged in positions that spoke of desperate combat and sudden defeat.
Some had fallen while trying to flee.
Others had died mid-attack, their offensive postures frozen by death before they could complete their strikes.
Three bore Rhyacian Tier classifications based on their residual authority.
Four had been Calymmian.
All of them were dead now!
Anaximander stood near the edge of the clearing with his arms crossed at all this violence.
Tairiyya floated nearby.
She said nothing, but her attention remained fixed on their leader.
THE Creature himself knelt beside one of the fallen Calymmian entities.
His hands were buried wrist-deep in the corpse’s chest cavity, having torn through Proterozoic Bones and flesh to reach what lay beneath.
Blood coated his arms up to the elbows, thick and dark and still carrying warmth from the life it had recently supported.
His expression held nothing but focus as he worked.
He pulled out a heart.
The organ was massive, and it pulsed with residual authority despite its owner’s death.
Proterozoic classification had transformed it into something far beyond mere muscle and blood vessels.
It was a repository of power, a concentrated source of everything its original owner had cultivated across eons of existence!
THE Creature brought it to his mouth and bit!
He chewed slowly and deliberately, savoring the authority that flooded into his existence with each swallow.
When he finished the heart, he reached back into the corpse for other organs.
Lungs came next, their Proterozoic structure providing different flavors of authority than the heart had offered.
Then the liver.
Then the kidneys.
Each organ consumed added to what THE Creature was becoming, each bite pushing him further along whatever path he had chosen when he burned away his Primordial Architect classification!
It was during this brutal feast that the sky above THE Wyld changed.
THE Creature raised his head, blood dripping from his chin as his eyes fixed on something that hadn’t been there moments before.
An illusory Pillar stretched across the sky!
Multicolored and banded with gold, it rose from somewhere far below and extended toward heights that even THE Wyld’s strange geometry couldn’t contain.
The Pillar blazed with power that pressed against everything nearby!
Anaximander looked up at the same moment, his eyes widening with surprise.
"What... is that?"
THE Creature studied the Pillar for several long seconds as if he could see things others couldn’t.
Blood continued dripping from his chin as a smile spread across his features.
"It burns with Infinity."
He looked at Anaximander with eyes that held fire from arecently usedTHE Silurian Light.
"So it may just be the one you continue to worry about that I tell you not to worry about."
Anaximander blinked at this assessment, his surprise deepening as he looked back toward the Pillar still blazing across the sky.
THE Creature returned his attention to the corpse before him, reaching for another organ as he continued.
"When pushed, when bullied, when adversity presses down and down without mercy or pause..."
He tore out what might have been a Proterozoic spleen and examined it with clinical interest.
"It can awaken a bloody beast within.
And that bloody beast may become its own adversity for those who thought themselves the predators."
His smile grew sharper.
He bit into the spleen, chewing thoughtfully.
"Adversity breeds greatness.
I still wait to see if Erwin will bloom into something astounding from my pressure..."
THE Creature returned to his eating with renewed focus, the Pillar above beginning to fade as whatever power had manifested it settled back into its source.
The illusory structure grew translucent, then ghostly, then disappeared entirely as if it had never been there at all.
But everyone who had seen it would remember.
Everyone who had witnessed it would wonder!
Anaximander threw his head back and laughed.
The sound rang out across the primeval forest with joy that seemed inappropriate given the corpses surrounding them, but it was genuine!

chapters.title: Chapter 5119: THE First Infinite Scale! IV
paragraphs: As he looked at the Pillar that stretched out endlessly, Noah felt something fundamental shift within his existence.

It was as if he had opened floodgates he hadn’t known were closed. The concentration of Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force within him, which had seemed almost full mere moments ago, now felt like it could expand countless more times. His capacity hadn’t merely increased. The very concept of capacity had changed, transforming from a finite container into something that could grow without boundary!
This was what he had been missing.

This was what standing at the supposed peak of THE First Scale had denied him. A ceiling he couldn’t perceive had been pressing down on his potential, limiting what he could hold and channel and become. Now that ceiling was gone, shattered by the construction of something that had never existed before.
This was Infinitas Architectura!
But not really. Not yet!
Because he hadn’t begun building.

The Hadean Pillar of Infinity held infinite potential, but it was currently hollow. A grand structure with no contents. A monument to what could be rather than what was. Its multicolored surface blazed with authority that came from its nature rather than its substance, potential rather than actualization.
Noah waved his hand.
The Pillar’s endless nature, which had stretched across all of Observable Existence moments before, began to fade.
What remained was a Pillar the height of this Oceanus-like realm he occupied, its form contained within THE Infiniverse rather than bleeding across everything that existed.
He looked down.

On the island far below, between the twin seas that stretched above and beneath, Naldine was looking up with a stern expression. Her singularity-dotted eyes studied the Pillar with attention that held something between analysis and wariness. She was trying to gauge his power, trying to understand what she had just witnessed!
Let her wonder.
Inside that blinding hollow Pillar of Infinity, Noah floated toward its base.

The interior was vast beyond comprehension, space that somehow existed within his existence while also occupying physical territory in the realm around him. The walls curved away in every direction, multicolored surfaces that awaited the Civilizations he would actualize upon them. But the floor was where everything would begin. The foundation upon which all else would be built.
"At the base of all of it will be Mana."
His voice emerged with conviction that pressed against the hollow interior.
"THE First Tongue."
HUUM!
The base of this glorious Pillar would have nothing except the one thing he had always possessed. The one constant across every transformation, every advancement, every impossible achievement.
THE First Tongue had been his Civilization before he knew what Civilizations were.
It would be his foundation now.
Noah knelt down at the base of his Pillar.

From his hands, endless blue light permeated outward. It wasn’t mere illumination but something far more fundamental, the very essence of what THE First Tongue represented made visible through his intention. Infinite absolute Seals began manifesting around him, weavings of authority that represented the twenty-seven Phonemes that comprised the foundational language of existence.
They gushed out endlessly, these Seals, as if they were seeds being planted on the very base of this Pillar of Infinity.

The twenty-seven letters formed into Logos. Into words. They mixed into each other countless times, creating variations and combinations that multiplied beyond what simple mathematics could describe. Each Phoneme touched each other Phoneme, creating new meanings. Those meanings combined with other meanings, creating concepts. Philologies and Archai bloomed!
Those concepts intertwined with other concepts, creating authorities.
As if the seeds were blooming, the entire basal region of the Pillar began to transform.

Illusory blue seeds sprouted from the floor. They pushed upward through nothing, through potential space that hadn’t existed until they needed it to exist. Saplings emerged from those seeds, their forms crystalline and luminous, their branches reaching toward the hollow heights above. The saplings flourished into trees, their growth accelerating past what any natural process could achieve.
A forest of THE First Tongue rose around Noah.

The color blue began rising in concentration all around him. It climbed past his knees, his waist, his chest. It exceeded his height and continued climbing, the forest growing denser and grander with each passing moment. Trees of language stretched toward the Pillar’s interior heights, their branches heavy with words that hadn’t been spoken yet, their leaves inscribed with meanings that most beings couldn’t comprehend.
At the very peak of all of it, something began to form.
A radiant Grimoire of Hadean Lexicons bloomed into existence.

The book was massive, its cover blazing with multicolored light that declared its nature without need for explanation. Its pages fluttered endlessly, never settling on a single configuration, each flutter revealing new words and new meanings and new possibilities. It was the actualization of THE First Tongue.
The moment this occurred, everything changed.

Rivers of golden Observable Force surged into this basal floor from somewhere beyond the Pillar’s walls. Observable Force rushed toward the actualized Civilization with purpose that felt almost desperate. It permeated across everything, across every tree and every branch and every leaf and every word.
The Pillar of Infinity began to shine unfathomably bright.
|THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity has been established.|
Ruination’s voice emerged with wonder!

|The first Civilization has been actualized within its structure. THE First Tongue now exists as a permanent foundation. Its power flows through your Pillar continuously, contributing to everything built upon it.|
|You have officially stepped onto Infinitas Architectura, The Infinite Architecture, of THE First Infinite Scale of Existence.|
|Your methodology has officially begun pioneering something new.|
|You deviate from Vakochev’s Scales of Existence.|
The words were grand ones.

Noah’s body inside his Pillar of Infinity radiated blinding light of brilliance that pressed against the crystalline forest surrounding him. His eyes shot out multicolored pillars of light that reached toward the Grimoire floating at the peak of his actualized foundation. Every aspect of his existence resonated with what he had just achieved.
Officially on his own path!
Deviating from Vakochev’s Scales of Existence!
At this point...
|Error.|
HUUM!
Ruination’s voice buzzed with caution that hadn’t been present moments before.
|New weavings of information from a foreign source incoming. Unable to stop them.|
Noah’s eyes became sharp as he sensed something pressing against his consciousness from outside.

Momentarily, Ruination’s voice and prompts faded. Her presence retreated as if pushed aside by something that possessed authority she couldn’t contest. In front of his eyes, in blue-bordered boxes and radiant blue letters that differed from Ruination’s golden notifications, new prompts bloomed.
A voice accompanied them.
It felt deep and ancient and heavy, carrying the weight of someone who had observed existence across spans that made eons seem like heartbeats. It wasn’t threatening. It wasn’t aggressive!
It simply was, the way mountains simply were, the way oceans simply were!
|...The path you have taken is an arduous and difficult one.|
The voice pressed against his consciousness with intensity!
|But it is welcomed.|
A pause that felt like centuries compressed into moments.

|The only thing I can tell you is to Persevere. Everything will stand in your way, but Persevere. Existence itself will oppose you, but Persevere. Enemies will seek your destruction, but Persevere. Allies will doubt your methods, but Persevere. Even family may stand in your way, questioning whether your path leads anywhere worth reaching.|
The voice grew heavier.
|Still, Persevere.|
Another pause.
|Osmont, right? Against all odds, against every force that will try to crush what you are building, against the weight of how things have always been...|
The ancient voice carried something that might have been respect.
|I, Vakochev, can only advise you to Persevere. And just maybe, if you succeed, I will see you in that place.|
The final word emerged with weight that shook his existence to its foundations.
|PERSEVERE!|
BOOM!
When that deep and ancient voice finished, Noah found his brows covered with sweat that shouldn’t have been possible for a Hadean Lifeform to produce!
His eyes shone fiercely as he processed what had just occurred. His nose breathed out flames of Infinity that scorched the crystalline trees nearest to him.
He...fully felt it now.
He had lost any connection he had with Vakochev’s Scales of Existence.

The framework that had governed power across Existence since before most current beings were born no longer applied to him. He couldn’t be measured by its standards because he had chosen to reject those standards entirely. The Scales that told everyone else where they stood and how far they had to go would tell him nothing.
He was very much alone.
A Pioneer, on his own!

chapters.title: Chapter 5120: Advancement! I
paragraphs: It is lonely at the top.
Such words have been uttered across countless civilizations and eons, spoken by beings who climbed higher than their peers and found themselves standing alone in territories no one else could reach!
But the loneliness of achievement pales in comparison to the loneliness of pioneering.

Those who reach the top of established paths at least have the comfort of knowing others have stood where they stand. They can look down and see the trail that led them upward, they can identify the footprints of predecessors who validated their journey through completion.They are alone in position but not in experience.
Pioneers have no such comfort.

They walk paths that do not exist until their feet touch ground. They climb mountains that have no peaks until they declare a stopping point. Every step is a question without a guaranteed answer, every advancement a gamble that could end in triumph or catastrophe with equal probability.
Who else can share their vision? By definition, no one!
No one!

If others could see what they see, the path would already exist. The Pioneer’s curse is to perceive possibilities that remain invisible to everyone else, to feel compelled toward destinations that others cannot even imagine. They speak of what they’re building and receive blank stares in return, confusion from those who cannot comprehend why anyone would abandon the safety of established routes.

And when Pioneers succeed, when they carve paths that others will eventually follow, those who come after will never understand what was required. They will walk the completed road and see only the road. They will not see the false starts, the collapsed tunnels, the chasms that nearly swallowed the one who built this passage. They will not know how many times the Pioneer considered turning back, how many moments of despair preceded each breakthrough, how much blood and sweat and tears soaked into foundations that now appear solid and inevitable.
The path will seem obvious in retrospect.
"Of course this was possible," they will say. "Of course someone would eventually do this."

But the Pioneer knew nothing was obvious. The Pioneer knew that "eventually" almost became "never" countless times during the construction. The Pioneer carries scars that the path’s future travelers will never see and could never appreciate!
This is the price of going first.
This...is what it means to be alone.
Noah felt a sense of emptiness settle into his existence.

It wasn’t pain or fear, just absence. He had belonged to some structure he couldn’t perceive before, some framework that had given him meaning and definition without his awareness. Vakochev’s Scales had been there like gravity, invisible but constant, telling him where he stood in relation to everything else. Now that definition was gone.

He could fall or stumble at any moment. There were no more markers telling him which direction was up. There was no more system declaring whether his next step would be advancement or regression. He floated in conceptual void where measurement itself had ceased to apply.
But in this lost sensation, he felt something else!
A glimmer of Infinity rising within him.
HUUM!

Infinity helped him up. Infinity kept him stable. The very foundation he had chosen to build upon refused to let him collapse into the emptiness that threatened to swallow him. It pressed against the void with authority that declared emptiness was just another form of potential, and potential was something Infinity understood intimately.
Because even though he did not have Vakochev’s Scales of Existence anymore, he was now forging his Infinite Scales of Existence!
His own framework. His own definitions. His own meaning!
HUUM!
Noah rose up sternly within his Hadean Pillar of Infinity.

He floated above the level where THE First Tongue had been actualized, past the crystalline forest of blue trees and the Grimoire of Hadean Lexicons that crowned its peaks. The foundation was complete. Now came the construction that would fill this hollow monument with substance worthy of its potential.
He looked upward toward the vast empty space that awaited the next Civilization.
"Existence."
His voice emerged calm and measured.
Below him, the actualized First Tongue responded to his call.

Blue Mana began flowing upward from the forest of language like endless water rising against gravity. It climbed through the Pillar’s interior in streams that wove around each other, rivers of THE First Tongue ascending toward the level where Noah floated. The blue light was beautiful in its purity, carrying the foundational authority of the language that underpinned all of reality.
Then it began to transform.

The blue started bubbling as if heated by invisible flames. Colors emerged from within the azure streams, reds and golds and greens and violets bleeding outward from cores that had been uniform moments before. The Mana was being elevated, THE First Tongue serving as the base material from which something grander would be forged.
The Civilization of Existence manifested as endlessly rising multicolored flames.

They didn’t burn the way normal fire burned. They declared that things were rather than were not. The flames rose in columns and curtains and spiraling towers, their heat carrying the warmth of reality itself pressing against the void of non-being. It looked like a forge! A cosmic forge where existence itself was hammered into shape from raw potential.
When the actualization completed, the second level of his Pillar blazed with authority that made THE First Tongue seem gentle by comparison.
Noah floated within those multicolored flames without discomfort.

"Existence...is not separate from Infinity," he said, his tone thoughtful and precise. "Infinity makes Existence possible by providing the endless potential from which reality emerges. And Existence gives Infinity meaning by actualizing that potential into something that matters. They need each other. One without the other is incomplete."
He paused, watching the flames dance around him.

"This is why they belong in the same Pillar. They are not separate foundations competing for primacy, they are aspects of the same fundamental truth. The Oldest Paradox understood this. I understand it now."
HUUM!

The flames of Existence settled into stable weavings as Observable Force and Infinity surged through them, golden rivers binding this second Civilization to the first. The Pillar grew brighter, its hollow interior now holding two levels of actualized authority stacked upon each other.
Noah rose higher.

He passed through the multicolored flames of Existence, their heat parting around him like water around a stone. Above them, more empty space awaited. More potential crying out for actualization! More levels to be built before his Pillar would approach anything resembling completion.
"Paradox."
The word emerged with the same deliberation he had used before.
Below, THE First Tongue and Existence responded together.

Blue Mana rose from the forest of language, climbing through the flames of Existence and absorbing their multicolored authority as it passed. The streams that emerged above the second level held both the foundational nature of THE First Tongue and the creative heat of Existence, combined into something that vibrated with tension between contradictory states.
The transformation began differently this time.

Rather than bubbling into new colors, the ascending streams started splitting. Each river of combined authority divided into two rivers flowing in opposite directions while somehow remaining in the same space. They contradicted themselves visually, logically, fundamentally. They were and were not. They moved and remained still. They existed in multiple states simultaneously because Paradox refused to accept that only one state could be true.
The Civilization of Paradox manifested as infinite reflections facing each other.

Mirrors made of crystallized contradiction stretched across this level of the Pillar, each one showing images that shouldn’t have been possible. Noah saw himself in one mirror as a human throwing fireballs. In another, as THE Youngest standing before a shadowy THE Deliverance. In a third, as something he hadn’t become yet, forms that existed only in potential futures that may or may not arrive. All of them were him. None of them were him. The Paradox refused to resolve!
Oh!

"Paradox...is Infinity’s closest sibling,"Noah observed, his voice steady despite the impossible reflections surrounding him. "Both reject limitation. Both insist that boundaries are suggestions rather than laws. The difference is that Infinity achieves the impossible by having no end, while Paradox achieves it by holding contradictions together until they stop being contradictions."
He looked at a mirror showing himself failing, then at one showing himself succeeding.
"I’ve learned to appreciate Paradox. It taught me that being weak and strong simultaneously is...a grand strategy."
HUUM!

sentences.text: It is lonely at the top.
Such words have been uttered across countless civilizations and eons, spoken by beings who climbed higher than their peers and found themselves standing alone in territories no one else could reach!
But the loneliness of achievement pales in comparison to the loneliness of pioneering.
Those who reach the top of established paths at least have the comfort of knowing others have stood where they stand.

They can look down and see the trail that led them upward, they can identify the footprints of predecessors who validated their journey through completion.They are alone in position but not in experience.
Pioneers have no such comfort.
They walk paths that do not exist until their feet touch ground.
They climb mountains that have no peaks until they declare a stopping point.
Every step is a question without a guaranteed answer, every advancement a gamble that could end in triumph or catastrophe with equal probability.
Who else can share their vision?
By definition, no one!
No one!
If others could see what they see, the path would already exist.
The Pioneer’s curse is to perceive possibilities that remain invisible to everyone else, to feel compelled toward destinations that others cannot even imagine.
They speak of what they’re building and receive blank stares in return, confusion from those who cannot comprehend why anyone would abandon the safety of established routes.
And when Pioneers succeed, when they carve paths that others will eventually follow, those who come after will never understand what was required.
They will walk the completed road and see only the road.
They will not see the false starts, the collapsed tunnels, the chasms that nearly swallowed the one who built this passage.

They will not know how many times the Pioneer considered turning back, how many moments of despair preceded each breakthrough, how much blood and sweat and tears soaked into foundations that now appear solid and inevitable.
The path will seem obvious in retrospect.
"Of course this was possible," they will say.
"Of course someone would eventually do this."
But the Pioneer knew nothing was obvious.
The Pioneer knew that "eventually" almost became "never" countless times during the construction.
The Pioneer carries scars that the path’s future travelers will never see and could never appreciate!
This is the price of going first.
This...is what it means to be alone.
Noah felt a sense of emptiness settle into his existence.
It wasn’t pain or fear, just absence.
He had belonged to some structure he couldn’t perceive before, some framework that had given him meaning and definition without his awareness.
Vakochev’s Scales had been there like gravity, invisible but constant, telling him where he stood in relation to everything else.
Now that definition was gone.
He could fall or stumble at any moment.
There were no more markers telling him which direction was up.
There was no more system declaring whether his next step would be advancement or regression.
He floated in conceptual void where measurement itself had ceased to apply.
But in this lost sensation, he felt something else!
A glimmer of Infinity rising within him.
HUUM!
Infinity helped him up.
Infinity kept him stable.
The very foundation he had chosen to build upon refused to let him collapse into the emptiness that threatened to swallow him.
It pressed against the void with authority that declared emptiness was just another form of potential, and potential was something Infinity understood intimately.
Because even though he did not have Vakochev’s Scales of Existence anymore, he was now forging his Infinite Scales of Existence!
His own framework.
His own definitions.
His own meaning!
HUUM!

He floated above the level where THE First Tongue had been actualized, past the crystalline forest of blue trees and the Grimoire of Hadean Lexicons that crowned its peaks.
The foundation was complete.
Now came the construction that would fill this hollow monument with substance worthy of its potential.

chapters.title: Chapter 5121: Advancement! II
paragraphs: The mirrors of Paradox settled, their contradictions stabilizing into patterns that shouldn’t have been stable. Infinity and Observable Force flowed through them, blue and golden binding agents connecting this third level to everything below. The Pillar blazed brighter still.
Noah rose again.
Three levels complete. One more to go before the foundation of his Hadean Pillar of Infinity would hold all four Aspects of THE Oldest Paradox in Existence!
"Chaos."
The final word fell into the Pillar’s interior with weight that belied its simple pronunciation.
Everything below responded.

Blue Mana from THE First Tongue. Multicolored flames from Existence. Contradictory reflections from Paradox. All of it rose together, streams and fires and mirrors ascending in combinations that grew more unstable with each passing moment. The authority climbing toward this final level held everything that had come before, all the foundational aspects combining into something that threatened to tear itself apart at any moment.
That was the point.
The transformation was violent!
Chaotic!

The ascending authority didn’t bubble or split. It exploded. It collapsed. It reformed in configurations that lasted milliseconds before shattering into new configurations equally temporary. Nothing held. Nothing stabilized. Nothing accepted the concept of permanence because Chaos refused to acknowledge that anything should remain the same for longer than it chose to.
The Civilization of Chaos manifested as an eternal storm.

Lightning made of pure possibility arced between clouds made of dissolved certainty. Winds carrying fragments of reality that had been torn apart howled through this level of the Pillar without pattern or purpose. Everything was destruction. Everything was creation!
The distinction between the two ceased to exist because Chaos saw no difference between breaking and building.
Noah stood at the center of the storm, his Hadean body untouched by devastation that would have erased lesser beings.

"Chaos is what Infinity looks like when you remove all the rules."His voice cut through the howling winds with calm that seemed inappropriate. "Pure potential without direction. Endless possibility without preference. Most beings fear Chaos because they need structure to feel safe. I’ve learned that Chaos isn’t the enemy of structure. It’s the raw material from which structure is built."
He watched reality fragment and reform around him.

"You can’t create anything truly new from order alone. You need Chaos to break the old patterns before new ones can emerge. THE Oldest Paradox understood this. Chaos isn’t the end. It’s the beginning that never stops beginning."
HUUM!
The storm of Chaos settled into patterns that weren’t really patterns, stable instability that somehow maintained itself through constant change.
The Pillar blazed with brilliance that could have blinded beings across multiple realms.
Noah floated upward.
He rose above the Hadean Pillar of Infinity and looked down at what he had built.

At its base, the crystalline forest of THE First Tongue spread blue light upward. Above that, the multicolored flames of Existence burned in their cosmic forge. Higher still, the contradictory mirrors of Paradox reflected impossibilities. And at the current peak, the eternal storm of Chaos raged without end.
The four Aspects of THE Oldest Paradox in Existence now lay within his Pillar.
THE First Tongue. Existence. Paradox. Chaos.

The foundational Civilizations that had defined power across Observable Existence since before most current beings were born. The Aspects that separated true claimants of THE Oldest Paradox from everyone else.
All of them, actualized within his Hadean Pillar of Infinity!
All of them, permanently integrated rather than temporarily accessed.

Noah looked upon this with a calm gaze, his expression holding satisfaction but not arrogance. What he had built was grand, but grandness wasn’t the point. Utility was the point. Foundation was the point!
Everything that followed would be built upon this, and everything that followed would determine whether his Infinite Scales of Existence meant anything at all.
"What came first?"
His voice emerged, posing the question to himself.
"THE First Tongue? Existence? Paradox? Chaos? Everyone wants to know which foundation is the true foundation, which beginning is the real beginning."
He looked at his Pillar, at the four levels stacked upon each other in the order he had chosen.
"But they’re asking the wrong question."
His eyes blazed like singularities.

"I emerged first before ushering them in. My will actualized them in the order I chose. My authority gave them form within my existence. THE Infinite Cause came first, and the rest of them followed. They exist in my Pillar because I put them there. They serve my progression because I decided they would!"
His voice remained steady, as if he were simply stating facts!
"The answer to what came first is always the same. The one doing the building came first. Everything else is just material."
BOOM!
Noah flew upward through his Hadean Pillar of Infinity, leaving the four foundational Civilizations behind as he rose toward the vast hollow space that awaited filling.
The base was complete! But foundations were just beginnings. What he built upon them would determine whether his Infinite Scales of Existence meant anything at all.
He didn’t slow down.
"The Civilization of Quintessence."

The words left his mouth as blue and multicolored authority surged upward from below, answering his call before he finished speaking. The actualization happened faster than it had with the foundational Aspects, his Pillar learning what he wanted and responding with increasing efficiency!
Quintessence settled into place as a layer of crystallized colorless potential, shimmering with authority.
He rose higher without pause.
"Loot."

Another layer actualized, this one manifesting as cascading streams of golden abundance that flowed endlessly without depleting. The Civilization that had defined so much of his early journey, that had given him access to rewards others couldn’t dream of claiming, now became permanent foundation within his existence!
"Cheats."

The layer that formed held configurations that shouldn’t have been stable, rules bent into shapes that favored him specifically. It settled into his Pillar with the comfortable familiarity of an old companion.
"Protagonist."

A layer of narrative weight, of causality that leaned in his direction, of events arranging themselves around his presence rather than despite it. This Civilization had been with him since before he understood what Civilizations were.
Noah continued ascending, his voice steady and unhurried despite the speed of his construction.
"Manadynamics. Relativity. Megalos. Outerversal."

Four more layers actualized in rapid succession, each one adding substance to the hollow interior of his Pillar. The authority flowing up from his foundation grew denser with each Civilization he called, the combined weight of everything below feeding everything above.
"Kuklos. Singed. Ordo Ab Chao."
The Pillar began to light up around him.

What had been merely bright before became something approaching blinding, multicolored radiance pressing outward through walls that struggled to contain the accumulating authority. Noah felt his existence responding to what he was building, felt weight settling into aspects of himself that had seemed free and unbound moments before!
This was different from freedom, he realized!
"Farming. Smithing. Devouring."

More layers. More weight! His Pillar stretched higher as he filled it, the hollow space above him shrinking with each Civilization actualized. The feeling of unboundedness that had followed his disconnection from Vakochev’s Scales began transforming into something else entirely.
"Helios. Dreams. Prana."

He was becoming heavy in ways that had nothing to do with physical mass. Every Civilization added to his foundation made him more present, more defined, more real in the fabric of Observable Existence!
The emptiness he had felt after hearing Vakochev’s message was being filled by construction that demanded his full attention.
"Avalon. Oceanus. Muspelheim. Jotunheim. Niflheimr. Alfheimr."
Realms that existed became permanent Civilizations of his Pillar, their authorities now integrated rather than merely contained. He could feel his internal reality resonating with each actualization!
"Limitless Existence. Silent Tongue. Radiant Paradox. Ordered Chaos."

Variations of his foundational Aspects settled into higher levels of his Pillar, permutations that expressed different facets of the same fundamental truths. THE First Tongue had spawned Silent Tongue. Existence had birthed Limitless Existence. Paradox gave rise to Radiant Paradox. Chaos produced Ordered Chaos.
The Pillar blazed with glory that pressed against everything nearby.
Noah continued building!
Like this, time began to pass!

chapters.title: Chapter 5122: Advancement! III
paragraphs: He had less than twenty-four hours before the Civilizational Holy War would begin, before his mother and son and everyone else he cared about would be pulled into isolated arenas to face Primordial Architects. The pressure of that deadline should have made him rush and should have introduced desperation into his actions.
But he had been doing something important through his Hadean Mind of Infinite Calculation.

Whenever he needed to think through a problem, whenever he encountered complexity that required extended contemplation, he could stop time for his perception alone. An instant could become infinite for his consciousness while the external world remained frozen. If he found himself stuck on any thought process or possibility, he simply paused for what felt like hours or days within that moment of perceptual infinity.
Then he resumed, having worked through whatever had given him pause with boundless solutions!
The construction continued.

Other bodies of his moved through THE Infiniverse simultaneously, carrying out preparations that couldn’t wait for his primary form to finish building. The mass transformation project that had begun before the Civilizational Holy War’s declaration now accelerated with urgency.
The first and major task was clear.

The vast majority of those closest and strongest within THE Infiniverse needed to attain Nascent Hadean classification. Not because it would guarantee their survival in the coming battles, but because it would give them a fighting chance against opponents who had spent eons cultivating power that most First Scale beings couldn’t comprehend.
One by one, they underwent transformation.

Existential Engineering flooded Observable Force and Quintessence Infiniforce into their existences. The Lattice of Foundational Constraint that defined Bounded Lifeforms shattered within them, replaced by the Lattice of Nascent Emergence that declared them something new!
Golden cracks appeared on foreheads. Dark hair developed rivers of gold. Eyes shifted toward hues that spoke of authority exceeding their previous classifications.
This...was all accomplished in the first hour.
Exactly twenty-three hours before The Civilizational Holy War.

Noah stood on a floating platform within a realm of THE Infiniverse that had taken the qualities of an endless training ground. The space stretched in every direction without visible boundary, its floor solid enough to support combat while its atmosphere hummed with Observable Force dense enough to accelerate recovery.
Naldine Manthon came at him with everything she had.

Her form blazed with authority that would have made her old self seem dim by comparison. She had used her Hadean Infinity of Development three times in rapid succession, each usage accelerating her progressionridiculously. Her bones no longer pulsed with merely Proterozoic light. They shone with the crystalline brilliance of full Hadean classification.
All two hundred and six of them.
All seventy-eight organs.

She had become the third most powerful being in THE Infiniverse, exceeded only by Noah himself and of course THE Infiniverse as a whole. In the span of hours, she had achieved what should have required eons of dedicated cultivation.
And yet.
Noah swatted her aside with casual ease.
BOOM!

He hadn’t exhibited any Infinity. Hadn’t channeled any Observable Force. He simply stood there with his hands clasped behind his back, his expression holding mild interest as she attacked with waves and seas of Quintessence Infiniforce that should have overwhelmed anyone at her former classification.
Her Hadean skeletal structure blazed through her skin as she struck.
He knocked her back with a gesture that seemed almost lazy.

Naldine skidded across the waters, her feet carving furrows into material that shouldn’t have yielded to anything. Frustration painted itself across her features without her permission, ancient pride warring with the reality that she couldn’t touch him no matter what she attempted.
"This doesn’t make sense," she said, her voice tight. "A Calymmian Proterozoic Scale entity would be crushed under me, and yet...You’re not even using your authority."
"I don’t need to."
His response was simple, stating fact rather than boasting!

Her singularity-dotted eyes blazed brighter as she shifted stance. If raw power wouldn’t work, perhaps something more refined would serve. Her hands began moving through motions that Noah recognized immediately, fingers curling and releasing in patterns that spoke of authority derived from THE Silurian Cause itself.
The somatic expression of THE Silurian Light.
Her voice emerged with weight that pressed against the training ground around them.
"Silurian Ember, First of Flames. I grasp the Thread. I burn the Thread. What was shall be unwritten, what stood shall stand no more."
Magma-like brilliance gathered between her palms.
"THE SILURIAN LIGHT."
The Pulse erupted toward him with force that had threatened to erase his existence not long ago.
Noah smiled.
He let it hit him.

The flames of THE Silurian Light washed over his form with heat that could have unmade Rhyacian entities through proximity alone. It pressed against his Hadean Dermis, against bones and organs that had been forged through countless cycles of destruction and rebirth caused by this very Pulse.
It felt warm.
Almost pleasant, like standing near a comfortable fire on a cold evening.
Then he breathed in.
HUUM!

The flames of THE Silurian Light flowed into his mouth, drawn by intention that exceeded what the Pulse had been designed to handle. He consumed the fire that Grimvault had used to threaten him, that Naldine now wielded. The brilliance vanished into him as if it had never existed.
He exhaled, and only faint embers emerged from his nostrils before fading entirely.
Naldine stared at him.
Her expression shifted through several emotions before settling on something between disbelief and reluctant acceptance. She shook her head slowly, white hair swaying with the motion.
"You monster."
The words held no real venom. Just acknowledgment of what she was observing.
Then her eyes flashed sharply, and something changed in her bearing.

If she couldn’t beat him in this sort of battle, there were other arenas where she might gain some measure of control. Other methods of contest where raw power mattered less than technique and will and the particular intimacies that Dual Cultivation demanded.
Her gaze filled with defiance that hadn’t been present moments before.
"Let’s switch to Cultivation." Her voice carried challenge that pressed against the space between them. "I refuse to believe you are this far away."
A Primordial Architect remained defiant despite evidence that should have crushed such defiance entirely.
But she would learn later on.
She was fighting against someone walking an entirely different Scale of Existence!
Noah looked at himself and what he was becoming.

His Hadean Pillar of Infinity continued filling with actualized Civilizations, each layer adding weight and definition to his existence within Infinitas Architectura. The second demarcation of his First Infinite Scale of Existence was taking shape around him, authority accumulating rapidly.
He didn’t bother trying to gauge exactly how easily he could defeat a Calymmian Proterozoic Scale entity anymore.

The exercise seemed pointless. Whenever he sparred with Naldine, who was many times more powerful than any Calymmian entity he had encountered, she couldn’t get past the defenses of his skin. Not his bones. Not his organs. Just his skin!
She attacked with everything her newly Hadean existence could muster, and his outermost layer of defense treated her efforts as irrelevant.

He would come to know in the distant future that wasn’t truly so distant exactly what his power was. There would be battles that tested him properly, enemies that forced him to reach for capabilities he hadn’t yet explored. THE Deliverance and whatever forces served that ancient being would eventually provide the pressure he needed to understand his own limits.
But as of right now, he was building toward something else entirely.

He wanted to forge himself to be so astoundingly different and exceptional that those who followed Vakochev’s Scales of Existence wouldn’t even know where to begin when it came to understanding him. Let them try to measure him against their frameworks. Let them attempt to categorize what he was becoming. They would find nothing that fit because he had chosen to exist outside their definitions!
More Civilizations actualized within his Pillar as he continued his work.

The main threshold he approached was the transition from Uncountable Infinity to Absolute Infinity. That advancement would mark his readiness to progress toward the third demarcation, toward Infinitas Causa where THE Infinite Cause itself would be fully comprehended and actualized. But such transitions couldn’t be rushed, couldn’t be forced through sheer will alone.
So while he continued building, another body of his focused on the second phase of strengthening his people.

The eighty-one who would be involved in the Civilizational Holy War needed more than Nascent Hadean classification to survive what was coming. They needed to forge their bones and organs to become fully Hadean. Naldine had demonstrated what that transformation meant in practical terms, her power increasing by orders of magnitude through aggressive application of Hadean Infinity of Development.
If his people could achieve similar results, they should be able to contend with Calymmian Proterozoic Scale entities.
They should be able to survive!
The Early Veiled Shore stretched beneath them in configurations of beauty that most beings would never witness.

Radiant gold sands sparkled under light that seemed to come from everywhere at once, their surfaces catching and reflecting the multicolored brilliance that saturated this region of THE Infiniverse. Endless plots of sacred herbs spread across the landscape in careful arrangements, their leaves and stems now burning with the light of Infinity that Noah’s presence had infused into everything within his internal reality.
The multicolored rain of THE Pluvial Epoch of Existential Infinity continued falling without pause.

It had caused river channels to form all across the Early Veiled Shore, waterways of liquid authority carving paths through golden sand and fertile soil. The rivers flowed with colors that shifted constantly, carrying Observable Force and Quintessence Infiniforce to territories that drank in whatever they received!
Noah floated in the skies above this paradise with dozens of his people surrounding him.

He gazed at Barbatos, whose dark gold eyes held anticipation beneath their calm surface. At Henry, his son, the young man’s blue gold hair shifting in winds that carried authority rather than mere air. At Adelaide, at Sigrid, at Riya, at Moiraine, at Titano, at THE Queen of Matter, at THE First Farmer, at Khor, at Tor, at THE Living Origin, at Ul’moreth, at Lumivara, at Skoll, at Ains, at THE Emperor Penguin, and many others whose existences had become intertwined with his own.
All of them waited for what he would say.

"We both have time and we don’t," Noah said, his voice calm and measured. "It depends on how we use what we’ve been given. Enemies far stronger than us are trying to collapse our very causality and existence. They declared war not because they fear what we are now, but because they fear what we might become."
He let that settle before continuing.

"In response, we won’t just be going for survival. We need to...dominate. We need to cause fear to spread across Observable Existence, so that nobody else could possibly think about doing something like this to us again."
His words pressed against everyone present!

"To ensure that reality, at the very least, all of you need to forge your Hadean Bones and Organs. One of the quicker ways for you to do that is an infusion of boundless Infinity and Observable Force, which I can provide."
He paused, his expression remaining steady.

"But you also need pressure to induce rapid transformation. External force that pushes your existence toward evolution. For that pressure, here is... a Primordial Architect that represents what those you will face will be like."
Noah waved his hand.
HUUM!

Golden light erupted from his palm as THE Hadean Desmoterion responded to his will. THE Hadean Organ of Civilization had continued to advance alongside everything else, allowing more and more things to become possible. Releasing powerful prisoners for limited durations was now a feasibility where it had once been beyond his capability.
A figure emerged from the golden light.
Beowulf materialized above the Early Veiled Shore with presence that pressed against everyone except Noah himself!

The Primordial Architect’s armored body stood massive and imposing, but something had changed since his imprisonment. His armor no longer held the colors it had displayed during their previous encounter. It now shone fully blue gold, the distinctive hue of Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force saturating every surface.
He had been disciplined in THE Hadean Desmoterion!

Ozymandias had worked on him in the dilated time that flowed differently within that prison, infusing him with Quintessence Infiniforce across spans that felt like years . The titanic form of Noah’s second body had transformed Beowulf into something he hadn’t been before.
A Nascent Hadean Lifeform.
|Beowulf, THE Primordial Architect of Armed Existence.|
|Classification: THE Second Scale of Vakochev’s Scales of Existence. Nascent Hadean Lifeform.|
|Skeletal Structure: 178 bones at Proterozoic classification. 28 bones at Hadean classification.|
|Organ Systems: 61 organs at Proterozoic classification. 17 organs at Hadean classification.|
|Current power output exceeds his previous parameters by a factor of approximately 127. Estimated classification now surpasses Grimvault at Calymmian Tier.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5123: Ego! I
paragraphs: The power emanating from Beowulf was more than a hundred times greater than what Noah had faced during their original confrontation. The Primordial Architect who had attacked with intent to claim his Infinity had been transformed into something far grander through imprisonment and forced cultivation.
But the eyes behind that empty armored helm held no pride in this advancement.
They held fear.
Immense, undeniable fear when they turned toward Noah!
Noah didn’t look at this fucking rat.
He simply waved his right hand again.
HUUM!
Another figure emerged from THE Hadean Desmoterion, this one taking form with presence that somehow exceeded even what Beowulf displayed.
THE Living Elemental materialized beside the armored Primordial Architect.

His form shifted through configurations of fire and water and earth and air, elemental authority that had been refined through the same process Beowulf had undergone. Blue gold light saturated every aspect of his constantly changing existence, Quintessence Infiniforce and Observable Force having been integrated so thoroughly that it had become part of what he fundamentally was.
|THE Living Elemental.|
|Classification: THE Second Scale of Vakochev’s Scales of Existence. Nascent Hadean Lifeform.|
|Skeletal Structure: 156 bones at Proterozoic classification. 50 bones at Hadean classification.|
|Organ Systems: 52 organs at Proterozoic classification. 26 organs at Hadean classification.|
|Current power output exceeds Beowulf by approximately 23%. Among the stronger Nascent Hadean entities currently in existence outside of your direct lineage.|
When THE Living Elemental finished materializing, his elemental form turned toward Noah.

Fear painted itself across features that shifted between states too quickly for most to track. The same fear that Beowulf displayed, the same recognition of what stood before them and what that presence meant for their continued existence.
Noah looked at THE Living Elemental with distaste that didn’t need to be hidden.

"The armored Primordial Architect will give you a glimpse of the ones you’ll fight,"he said, his voice remaining calm despite the expression on his face. "And this shitty, good for nothing Living Elemental is another Second Scale you can struggle against."
His gaze swept across his gathered people.
"I would have acted as the one to fight against you all, but I haven’t fully gauged my own strength yet. I don’t want to accidentally collapse you all while sparring."
A pause that felt almost casual.
"So for now, just hang on with these trash enemies. Once I’ve fully acclimated to my power, you’ll all face me."
Incredulous reactions rippled through the gathered crowd.
Barbatos smiled wryly, her dark gold eyes holding amusement.
Others looked at Beowulf and THE Living Elemental with something approaching pity.
This was a Primordial Architect who had existed for eons, who had accumulated power that most beings couldn’t comprehend!
And Noah called him trash!
Training dummies for his people to sharpen themselves against.
HUUM!
Terrifying power bloomed from the two released prisoners as they prepared for what was about to occur.

They moved with fear driving every action, because they understood something that Noah’s people were only beginning to grasp. If they didn’t sufficiently accomplish what they had been brought out here to do, if they failed to provide adequate pressure for transformation, if they were deemed useless for even this purpose...
Once they returned to that prison where time moved extremely differently, they would be punished for years.
Ozymandias was waiting, and Ozymandias had learned new methods of discipline during his own transformation!
Twenty hours remained until the Civilizational Holy War.
Noah was overseeing many things across THE Infiniverse when part of his consciousness received a tug of emotions. He frowned at the sensation. A moment later, he sent a body out to investigate.
The location was a distant place in the endless Wastes.

He appeared in a region that had become a swirling multicolored sea due to the Quintessence Infiniforce saturating everything. The waters churned without pattern, colors bleeding into each other. Half submerged in these impossible seas, a massive shattered Shelter of THE Loom rose from the depths like the corpse of a fallen giant.
The structure had been destroyed!
Atop the shattered Shelter, a figure materialized.

THE Living Emotive didn’t appear as an illusory visage gathered from ambient emotions this time. Her existence was fully present, an accumulation of feelings so dense and real that she pressed against the surrounding environment simply by being there. Chaos swirled around her form in visible currents, authority she had claimed mixing with the emotional resonance that defined her nature.
She was manically beautiful.

Her features held symmetry, every angle and curve designed to draw attention and hold it captive. But there was something wrong with that beauty, something manic beneath its surface that made appreciation feel like a trap. Her smile stretched too wide when she looked at him!
Her hair shifted colors as he watched.

It moved through shades that corresponded to nothing external, responding instead to emotions that flickered through her existence faster than most beings could track. Red bled into violet bled into gold bled into black, the transitions happening without pattern or warning. One moment she seemed wreathed in passion, the next in something closer to despair, the next in triumph that had no apparent source.
Noah’s gaze remained cold as she looked at him and smiled brilliantly.
"You..anh, you detest me..."
Her voice carried weavings that pressed against his consciousness, each word layered with emotional weight that would have influenced lesser beings.
She was not so manic as last time. Her words were more coherent!

"I can feel it, you know. That emotion! The distaste you hold for me radiates so strongly that I could locate you across Observable Existence simply by following its trail. Though you seem to be inside a place I cannot lock down as all emotions inside of it...are locked deeper than even THE Wyld..."
She stepped closer across the shattered surface of the Shelter, her bare feet leaving impressions that glowed with residual feeling.
"Most beings try to hide their emotions from me. But you don’t bother. You let me see exactly how much you wish I would disappear from your awareness entirely."
Her smile didn’t falter.

"I find that oh so refreshing. It is why right now...I pulled on my emotions of logic and coherence to speak oh so clearly to you. Do you like my words? Straightforward! Formal! And I havent rhymed anything just yet which is hard...ah!"
Noah said nothing, simply watching as she spoke.

"I should explain something,"she continued, her hair shifting through blues and greens. "My fixation on you isn’t arbitrary. It’s in my nature to become fixated on whoever controls the most emotions across Observable Existence at any given time. The being whose presence influences how others feel simply by existing."
She tilted her head, studying him with eyes that held too many colors simultaneously.

"That was Abaddon for a time. Then THE Creature, when he burned away his classification and began doing things that made even ancient entities feel fear. Then it was Erwin, THE Living Paradox, when his machinations began affecting the information that shapes how beings perceive their circumstances. "
Her smile sharpened.
"But now it’s you. It...has always been you! You’re like a beacon to me! A lighthouse that every emotional current eventually flows toward."
She paused, seeming to consider her next words carefully despite the manic energy that radiated from her.

"I know that history can interfere with future. What happened before and what I did before colors how you see me now. My actions towards Malphas and many others...Oh, and I even tried to kill you! Silly me! But hey, look at us now? Not too long ago, you slapped me until all my teeth fell out! Ahh.. I play that memory constantly to remember how much you detest me! So I will proceed slowly, carefully, in whatever manner causes you the least displeasure."
Her hair cycled through colors that suggested submission beneath their shifting surface.
"If you command me to kneel, I will kneel."
She knelt as she spoke, demonstrating rather than merely describing.
"If you command me to lick, to beg, to be a worm crawling at your feet, I would do it. If you command me to collapse myself entirely, to end my existence because my presence offends you..."
Her eyes met his from her kneeling position.
"Oh...fuck, I’m realizing now that I really might just do that too! Sheesh! That would not be too ideal but...oh! That is my nature when my fixation has become this strong. I cannot help what I am."
Noah’s expression didn’t change, but he continued listening.
THE Living Emotive rose from her kneel with fluid grace, her hair now settling into steadier shades of purple and silver.

"After claiming Chaos and siphoning the power of all emotions across Observable Existence, I changed tremendously. I gained access to understanding that had been hidden from me before. And I found out something pivotal."
Her voice grew more serious, the manic edge retreating slightly.

"For Primordial Architects and other lifeforms at THE Second Scale who want to infuse themselves with Infinity without going mad, the most critical factor is actually Ego. Their emotion. Their sense of self refined into something that can withstand pressure that would dissolve lesser consciousnesses."
She began pacing across the shattered Shelter, her words flowing with the cadence of genuine discovery.

"To go against the madness of Infinity, they amplify what they affirmed with their Civilizational Anchor. They further enhance and inflate certain emotions to be so strong within their Ego, within their existence, that they develop an unfathomably high resistance to Infinity depending on how amplified a singular or multiple emotions are."
Her pacing stopped as she turned to face him again.

"So I realized something that contradicted what I had always assumed. At the peak of power, you don’t find mindless sages who have attained some nirvanic state and abandoned all feeling. Emotions and the state of being are actually deemed unfathomably more critical at higher classifications. The conscious mind, the unconscious depths, the raw impulses of extremely powerful beings are all cultivated specifically to bear Infinity."
Her hair shifted through golds and whites as she spoke with increasing intensity.

"I found all of this out because the structure of THE Wyld became clear to me after I claimed Chaos and pulled on all emotions. Where power concentrates. How authority flows. The configurations that determine who rules and who serves."
Her eyes blazed brighter.

"THE Deliverance and three others of his stature rule THE Wyld. Four beings whose power exceeds everything beneath them by margins that make comparison meaningless. And THE Deliverance and these other top dogs, they have a direct connection to something grand. Something that provides them with advantages that Bounded Lifeforms shouldn’t be able to touch."
She stepped closer to Noah, her voice dropping lower.
"My fixation. My fascination. My...Anchor. The reason I came here despite knowing how much you detest me...was to give you information of those in the Civilizational Holy War, but also..."
Her hair settled into pure gold.
"Do you know about THE Gilded Ones?"
Noah stared at her coldly.

The distaste remained, rooted in history that couldn’t be erased through useful information. She had done things that earned his hatred, and no amount of kneeling or offering would change that foundation.
But he was pragmatic above all else.
And this being who disgusted him may just prove to be an anomaly more disgusting than Erwin or even come close to rival...THE Creature!?
